g1-q80.explanation: The white car is starting off from a parked position, while the yellow car is already moving and changing into the right lane. Starting off is a maneuver that must not obstruct other road users, and signaling with a turn indicator does not grant priority. Therefore, the driver of the white car yields (Rules, item 3, subitem 6; item 36).

g1-q81.text: A U-turn at the indicated location is:
options: Permitted if it does not interfere with public transit vehicle drivers.
g1-q81.explanation: Sign 5.16 "Bus and (or) Trolleybus Stop" is installed at the indicated spot. A U-turn is prohibited on sections of the carriageway where public transport stops are located, and this prohibition does not depend on whether you obstruct buses (Rules, item 50, sign 5.16).

g1-q82.text: Along which path is the left turn permitted?
g1-q82.explanation: Up to the intersection, the road is one-way, as indicated by signs 5.6 "End of One-Way Road" and 1.21 "Two-Way Traffic". Before turning left, a driver must take the far-left lane of the carriageway in advance, as in trajectory B, whereas along A the turn is made from the right lane (Rules, item 40, sign 5.6).

options: Has the right-of-way because the vehicle is approaching from the right.
g1-q83.explanation: The passenger car is entering the road via an acceleration lane and merging into the main lane. In this case, the driver must yield to vehicles travelling along the road—here, the truck. The rule of yielding to a vehicle approaching from the right applies only when the order of passage is not specified by the Rules, whereas here it is specified (Rules, items 45, 47).

g1-q84.text: Along which path is the right turn permitted?
g1-q84.explanation: When turning right, a vehicle must drive as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway. Trajectory A leads into the far-right lane of the intersecting road, whereas B swings wide into a lane farther to the left, which does not meet that requirement (Rules, item 41).

g1-q85.text: Along which path is the U-turn permitted?
g1-q85.explanation: A U-turn is prohibited on pedestrian crossings. Along trajectory B, the vehicle turns directly on the crossing marked by signs 5.19.1, 5.19.2 and "Zebra" marking, whereas along A the U-turn is performed past the crossing and along C before it. There is no prohibition in those places, so trajectories A and C are permitted (Rules, item 50, subitem 1).

g1-q86.text: In this situation, must the driver first change to the right lane and only then make the right turn?
g1-q86.explanation: Before turning right, a driver must occupy the far-right lane, except when turning from other lanes is also permitted by a sign or road marking. The arrow of marking 1.18 painted in the driver's lane permits proceeding straight and turning right, so the right turn may be made directly from this lane without changing to the right lane (Rules, item 40, subitem 2).

g1-q87.text: While on a bridge, is a U-turn permitted?
options: Permitted if visibility is 100 m or more.
g1-q87.explanation: A U-turn is prohibited on and under bridges, overpasses, and viaducts regardless of visibility. The 100 m visibility condition applies to other places, whereas on a bridge a U-turn is prohibited in all cases (Rules, item 50, subitem 3).

g1-q88.text: Entering the intersection from the indicated lane is:
options: Permitted only when making a U-turn.
g1-q88.explanation: The requirement to occupy an outer lane before turning or making a U-turn does not apply to entering a roundabout intersection. Here the intersection is marked with sign 4.3 "Roundabout", so you may enter it from the left lane as well to continue in any direction, not only for a U-turn. When entering, you must yield to traffic already moving in the roundabout (Rules, item 40, subitem 1; item 98.1).

g1-q89.text: Is a U-turn permitted at this location?
options: Permitted if visibility is 100 m or more.
g1-q89.explanation: The road section shown has a curve in the carriageway, but there are no signs prohibiting a U-turn and no solid road marking. Consequently, making a U-turn is permitted only on condition that road visibility in both directions is 100 m or more, which rules out unconditional "Yes" and "No" answers (Rules, item 50).

g1-q90.text: Must the driver proceeding straight ahead in the second lane yield to the driver changing lanes from the right?
g1-q90.explanation: A driver changing lanes must yield to vehicles travelling in the same direction in the adjacent lane without changing direction. The driver changing from the right lane with a left turn signal yields, while the driver going straight in their lane has no obligation to yield. The driver on the left yields only in the event of a simultaneous lane change (Rules, item 39).

g1-q91.text: A U-turn at this location is:
g1-q91.explanation: Sign 1.12.1 "Dangerous Curves" with plate 8.2.1 "Distance of Application" only warns of a 300 m dangerous section and does not prohibit a U-turn. Item 50 prohibits a U-turn, in particular, where visibility in at least one direction is less than 100 m. Here the road is clearly visible, the center line is broken, and there is no prohibiting sign, so a U-turn is permitted (Rules, item 50, subitem 5).

g1-q92.explanation: After turning left, you must not end up on the oncoming traffic side. In the image, both trajectories end on the side of the intersecting road intended for traffic in our direction, so turning left is permitted along either trajectory (Rules, item 41).

g1-q93.text: When starting to move simultaneously from a parking area, must you yield to the driver ahead?
g1-q93.explanation: When turning left in a parking lot, our path intersects the path of the opposite car, which is turning to its right. No order of passage is specified for such a situation, so the driver being approached from the right must yield. The opposite car is approaching us from the right, so we must yield (Rules, item 45).

g1-q94.text: In this situation, along which path is the driver permitted to make a left turn?
g1-q94.explanation: Sign 5.7.2 "Exit onto a One-Way Road" indicates that traffic on the intersecting road moves in one direction—to the left—and there is no oncoming traffic side. Therefore, after turning left, whether entering the near lane or the far lane, you will not end up on the oncoming side and may choose either trajectory (Rules, item 41, sign 5.7.2).

g1-q95.text: Is it permitted to make a U-turn at an intersection by backing?
options: Yes, if it does not interfere with traffic proceeding through the intersection.
g1-q95.explanation: Reversing is prohibited at intersections, so making a U-turn there by reversing is not permitted. The prohibition is unconditional: even if you do not obstruct traffic passing through the intersection, reversing is not allowed. The U-turn must be executed without reversing (Rules, item 49).

g1-q96.text: In this situation, is the driver permitted to make a right turn?
g1-q96.explanation: Before turning right, a driver must occupy the far-right lane unless turning from other lanes is permitted by a sign or marking. The driver is in the left lane, where there are no arrows or signs permitting a right turn, so the green arrow of the additional section does not give them the right to turn right from here; movement on that arrow is allowed from the far-right lane (Rules, item 40).

g1-q97.text: When stopping in this situation, which turn signal must the driver activate?
options: The right turn signal, and after changing lanes, the left turn signal.
g1-q97.explanation: Pulling over by changing lanes is a maneuver before which you must signal with the turn indicator of the corresponding direction. On a road marked with sign 5.5 "One-Way Road", stopping in a built-up area is also permitted on the left side, and the driver is changing lanes toward the left edge, so they must turn on the left indicator before starting the maneuver and turn it off after completing it (Rules, items 36, 79).

g1-q98.text: Indicate the path or paths along which traffic is permitted.
g1-q98.explanation: When turning right, a vehicle must drive as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway (sign 5.7.1 indicates that the intersecting road is one-way). Trajectory A leads into the far-right lane, while B leads into a farther lane, which does not meet this requirement. Driving straight along trajectory C is not prohibited here, so only trajectories A and C are permitted (Rules, item 41, sign 5.7.1).

g1-q99.text: When backing with insufficient visibility, the driver must:
g1-q99.explanation: Reversing is permitted provided it is safe and does not obstruct other road users, and if necessary the driver must seek assistance from other people. When nothing is visible behind, a horn or hazard warning lights do not make reversing safe, so you must ask for assistance (Rules, item 48).

g1-q100.text: In this situation, backing in order to enter the yard is:
g1-q100.explanation: The image shows sign 5.5 "One-Way Road". Reversing is prohibited in the places listed in item 50, including on one-way roads, so you may not reverse to enter a courtyard even if you do not obstruct anyone (Rules, items 49, 50, sign 5.5).

g1-q101.text: In this situation, making a U-turn by backing and using the yard entrance is:
options: Permitted if it does not interfere with other road users.
g1-q101.explanation: The image shows no place where reversing is prohibited—no intersection, pedestrian crossing, one-way road, or relevant sign. Reversing is permitted if it is safe and does not create an obstruction, so making a U-turn using a courtyard entrance is permitted provided no other road users are obstructed (Rules, items 48–50).

g1-q102.text: Is the passenger-car driver permitted to start moving?
options: Yes, if it does not interfere with the truck driver.
g1-q102.explanation: Starting off from the edge of the road is a maneuver, and a maneuver must not obstruct others. Signaling with a turn indicator does not grant priority, so the passenger car may move off only if doing so will not obstruct the approaching truck (Rules, item 36).

g1-q103.text: In which case is backing permitted?
options: In lanes other than the rightmost lane.
g1-q103.explanation: Reversing is prohibited at intersections, when exiting an adjacent area onto a road, and in the places listed in item 50, including on pedestrian crossings. There is no such prohibition for lanes other than the far-right lane, so reversing there is permitted if it is safe and does not obstruct other road users (Rules, items 48, 49, 50).

g1-q104.text: In this situation, is the driver permitted to proceed on the tram tracks?
options: Permitted only when making a U-turn or a left turn.
g1-q104.explanation: Before the intersection, signs 5.15.1 "Lane Directions" and 5.15.2 "Lane Direction" are installed. With such signs, driving on tram tracks at the intersection is prohibited, and the left turn is executed from the lane permitted by the sign rather than from the tram tracks (Rules, items 40, 59, signs 5.15.1, 5.15.2).

g1-q105.text: In this situation, when making a left turn, must the driver give a signal with the turn indicator?
options: Yes, when there is oncoming traffic.
g1-q105.explanation: Before turning, a driver is required to signal with the turn indicator of the corresponding direction regardless of whether there is oncoming traffic. Sign 4.1.6 only restricts the permitted directions and does not cancel the signaling requirement: the indicator informs all road users (Rules, item 36, sign 4.1.6).

g1-q106.explanation: After turning, you must not end up on the oncoming traffic side. The intersecting road has two-way traffic: trajectory A ends on our side of the center line, which after a left turn is the oncoming traffic side, whereas B leads beyond the center line. Therefore, turning left is permitted only along trajectory B (Rules, item 41).

g1-q107.text: Is the passenger-car driver permitted to approach the passenger on the bridge by backing?
options: Yes, if it does not interfere with other road users.
g1-q107.explanation: Reversing is prohibited in the places listed in item 50, including on bridges, overpasses, and viaducts. The prohibition is unconditional, so you may not reverse toward a passenger on a bridge even if it will not obstruct other road users (Rules, items 49, 50).

g1-q108.text: Is a U-turn permitted in this situation?
options: Permitted only if road visibility is more than 100 m.
g1-q108.explanation: The broken line of the road marking is on your side, so it may be crossed and the marking does not prohibit a U-turn. A U-turn is prohibited where road visibility in at least one direction is less than 100 m, so it is permitted only when visibility is 100 m or more (Rules, item 50, subitem 5; marking 1.11).

g1-q109.text: Which rule does the driver violate when entering the yard?
options: The driver makes a right turn within the area of effect of a “Straight Ahead Only” sign.
The driver does not activate the turn signal.
Both violations at the same time.
g1-q109.explanation: Sign 4.1.1 "Proceed Straight" does not prohibit turning right into courtyards and other areas adjacent to the road, so entering the courtyard itself is not a violation. However, entering a courtyard is a turn, and before doing so the driver must signal with the right turn indicator, which they fail to do (Rules, item 36; sign 4.1.1).

g1-q110.text: Must we yield to the truck driver?
options: Yes, if the driver has given a hand signal indicating this.
g1-q110.explanation: A gas station is an adjacent area, and a driver exiting from it onto the road must yield to vehicles travelling along the road. Therefore, we who are driving along the road are not required to yield to the truck, and giving a hand signal does not grant it priority (Rules, items 36, 38).

g1-q111.text: Along which path is the U-turn permitted?
g1-q111.explanation: Signs 5.19.1 and 5.19.2 show that there is a pedestrian crossing before the intersection, and a U-turn is prohibited on pedestrian crossings. Along trajectory B, the U-turn is made before the intersection on that crossing, whereas along A it is made in the intersection, where a U-turn is not prohibited here. Therefore, only trajectory A is permitted (Rules, item 50, subitem 1).

g1-q112.text: Along which path is the U-turn permitted?
g1-q112.explanation: A U-turn is prohibited only in the places listed in item 50: on pedestrian crossings, in tunnels, on bridges, at railway crossings, where visibility is less than 100 m, on sections with public transport stops, and on one-way roads. Both trajectories are outside those places (sign 5.7.2 applies to the intersecting road), so either trajectory is permitted (Rules, item 50).

g1-q113.explanation: The road narrows on the right (sign 1.20.2 "Road Narrows"), and the truck with its left turn signal on is changing into the passenger car's lane. The driver changing lanes must yield to vehicles travelling in the adjacent lane without changing direction, and a warning sign does not grant priority, so the truck driver yields (Rules, item 39).

g1-q114.text: After mistakenly entering an intersection, is it permitted to correct the maneuver by backing and then continue in the required direction?
g1-q114.explanation: Reversing is prohibited at intersections, so even after entering an intersection by mistake, correcting it by reversing is not permitted. You must continue driving and correct your route where doing so is permitted (Rules, item 49).

g1-q115.text: From this lane, traffic may continue:
options: To the left and by making a U-turn.
To the right, to the left, and by making a U-turn.
g1-q115.explanation: Sign 4.1.6 "Turn Right or Left" permits only those directions, and signs permitting a left turn also permit a U-turn. The driver is in the left lane, whereas a right turn must be made from the far-right lane because neither the sign nor road markings permit it from other lanes. Therefore, from this lane you may turn left or make a U-turn (Rules, item 40; sign 4.1.6).

g1-q116.text: In the indicated situation, is it permitted to back up in order to enter the yard by making a right turn?
options: Yes, if we do not interfere with public transit vehicle traffic.
g1-q116.explanation: Reversing is prohibited in the places listed in item 50, including on road sections with public transport stops: the stop sign and yellow road marking are visible in the image. Not creating an obstruction does not cancel the prohibition, so reversing to enter a courtyard is not allowed (Rules, items 49, 50).

g1-q117.text: In this situation, when changing to the adjacent lane:
options: You must yield to drivers proceeding in that lane.
g1-q117.explanation: When changing lanes, you must yield to vehicles travelling in the adjacent lane without changing direction. The arrow of marking 1.19 merely warns that the occupied lane is ending, and the right turn signal does not grant priority, so you must yield to the car driving in the right lane (Rules, items 36, 39, marking 1.19).

g1-q118.text: Along which path is the U-turn permitted?
g1-q118.explanation: Sign 3.18.2 prohibits only turning left, whereas a U-turn is a separate maneuver (which is prohibited by sign 3.19). A U-turn is prohibited in the places listed in item 50, and both trajectories are outside those places (the pedestrian crossing is past the intersection), so either trajectory is permitted (Rules, items 3, 50, sign 3.18.2).

g1-q119.text: Along which path is the left turn permitted?
g1-q119.explanation: After turning left, you must not end up on the oncoming traffic side. All three trajectories in the image end on the side intended for traffic in our direction, so turning left is permitted along any of them (Rules, item 41).

g1-q120.text: In this situation, is it permitted to approach the passenger by backing?
g1-q120.explanation: Reversing is permitted if it is safe and does not obstruct other road users. It is prohibited at intersections, when exiting an adjacent area onto a road, and in the places listed in item 50, none of which are present in the image. Sign 4.1.1 "Proceed Straight" sets the direction of travel, and reversing is not a change of direction (Rules, items 48 and 49, sign 4.1.1).

g1-q121.text: When making a left turn or U-turn outside an intersection, you must:
options: Yield to oncoming vehicles and to trams proceeding in the same direction.
g1-q121.explanation: When turning left or making a U-turn outside an intersection, the driver of a non-rail vehicle must yield not only to oncoming vehicles, but also to a tram travelling in the same direction. Yielding only to oncoming vehicles is not enough, as the rule separately specifies a tram moving in the same direction (Rules, item 44).

g1-q122.text: Is driving in reverse permitted in this situation?
options: Permitted up to the pedestrian crossing.
g1-q122.explanation: The image shows sign 5.5 "One-Way Road". Reversing is prohibited both on pedestrian crossings and on one-way roads. The prohibition applies along the entire road section, not only on the crossing, so reversing is not allowed before the crossing either (Rules, items 49, 50, sign 5.5).

g1-q123.text: When starting to move, must you yield to the driver making a U-turn?
g1-q123.explanation: Starting off from a parked position is a maneuver, and a maneuver must not obstruct others, nor does signaling grant priority. The oncoming car is already moving and making a U-turn, so when moving off you must yield to it (Rules, items 3, 36).

g1-q124.text: In this situation, approaching the passenger by driving in reverse is:
options: Permitted if it does not interfere with other drivers.
g1-q124.explanation: The situation takes place in a tunnel, and reversing is prohibited in the places listed in item 50, including in tunnels. Therefore, you may not reverse toward a passenger even if doing so does not hinder other drivers (Rules, items 49, 50).

g1-q125.text: Which driver violates the traffic rules when exiting the roundabout?
g1-q125.explanation: Before turning, a driver must occupy the appropriate outer lane in advance. The exception for a roundabout intersection applies only to entering it, not to exiting. The truck is exiting from the far-right lane, whereas the passenger car is exiting from the inner lane and crossing the truck's lane, so the passenger car driver is violating the rules (Rules, item 40, sign 4.3).

g1-q126.text: A U-turn at this intersection is:
g1-q126.explanation: Intersections are not among the places listed in item 50 where U-turns are prohibited (at intersections reversing is prohibited, not making a U-turn). Here there is no sign 3.19 or other prohibiting sign, and the solid line ends before the intersection, so a U-turn is permitted provided the rules for passing intersections are observed (Rules, items 49, 50).

g1-q127.text: In which direction is traffic permitted?
options: Straight ahead and to the left.
To the left and by making a U-turn.
g1-q127.explanation: The main red signal of the traffic light prohibits driving straight ahead, while the green arrow of the additional section permits a left turn, which is allowed from this lane by sign 5.15.1 and marking 1.18. Before making a U-turn, you must occupy the far-left lane (that sign and marking permit a U-turn only from it), whereas the car is in the right lane, so only a left turn is permitted (Rules, items 7, 8, 40, sign 5.15.1, marking 1.18).

g1-q128.text: Must you activate the right turn signal at this intersection?
options: Yes, except when making a U-turn.
g1-q128.explanation: Exiting a roundabout intersection is a right turn, and before any maneuver a signal is given with the indicator of the corresponding direction. Even if you are making a U-turn by going around the circle, you exit the intersection to the right, so the right turn signal is mandatory (Rules, items 3, 36, sign 4.3).

g1-q129.text: When entering an adjacent area, the driver must yield to:
options: Bicyclists and must not interfere with pedestrians.
g1-q129.explanation: When entering an adjacent area from a road, a driver must yield to cyclists and not obstruct pedestrians. The rule imposes both requirements simultaneously, so yielding only to pedestrians or only to cyclists is not sufficient (Rules, item 38).

g1-q130.text: When exiting an adjacent area, the driver must yield to:
options: Vehicles proceeding on the road and must not interfere with pedestrians.
g1-q130.explanation: When exiting an adjacent area onto a road, a driver must yield to vehicles travelling along the road and also not obstruct pedestrians. Taking only vehicles or only pedestrians into account is incomplete (Rules, item 38).

g1-q131.text: After this sign, making a U-turn is permitted:
options: Only if visibility is at least 100 m in both directions.
If it does not create an obstruction.
g1-q131.explanation: The image shows sign 5.5 "One-Way Road". On one-way roads, a U-turn is prohibited without exceptions, so it is not permitted even with 100 m visibility or when not obstructing anyone (Rules, item 50, sign 5.5).

options: Gives the driver right-of-way over other road users.
Gives the driver right-of-way only when changing lanes.
Does not give the driver right-of-way over other road users.
g1-q132.explanation: Giving a signal does not grant priority over other road users—neither when changing lanes nor during any other maneuver. A signal only warns of an intention, while the maneuver itself must not obstruct other road users (Rules, item 36).

g1-q133.text: The right turn along the indicated path is:
g1-q133.explanation: When turning right, a vehicle must drive as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway. In the far-right lane there is a car stopped with its hazard warning lights on, so moving into the adjacent lane here is precisely keeping as far right as possible, and turning along the indicated trajectory is permitted (Rules, item 41).

g1-q134.text: After passing the truck, in which lane is it permitted to continue?
options: In either lane proceeding in the same direction.
g1-q134.explanation: Outside built-up areas, drivers must keep as close as possible to the right edge of the carriageway, and occupying left lanes when right lanes are free is prohibited. After passing the truck, the right lane is free, so you must return to it and continue driving only in the right lane (Rules, item 55).

g1-q135.text: When turning into the yard, you must:
g1-q135.explanation: When entering a courtyard, a driver must yield to cyclists and not obstruct pedestrians. Both a cyclist and pedestrians are visible near the entrance in the image, so both requirements apply (Rules, item 38).

g1-q136.text: A U-turn at the indicated location is:
options: Permitted if no public transit vehicles are present.
g1-q136.explanation: The image shows sign 5.16 "Bus and (or) Trolleybus Stop". A U-turn is prohibited on sections of the carriageway where public transport stops are located, and the prohibition does not depend on whether there is a vehicle at the stop (Rules, item 50, sign 5.16).

g1-q137.text: If visibility of 100 m is provided in both directions, is it permitted to make a U-turn along the indicated path?
g1-q137.explanation: The indicated trajectory goes onto the right shoulder for the U-turn, and driving on the shoulder is prohibited. Visibility of 100 m permits a U-turn, but does not cancel that prohibition, so making a U-turn along this trajectory is not permitted (Rules, items 50, 61).

g1-q138.explanation: A gas station is an adjacent area. When exiting from there onto a road, a driver must yield to vehicles travelling along the road, so the driver of the truck travelling on the road has the right of way (Rules, item 38; Law, art. 2).

g1-q139.text: When changing lanes simultaneously, which vehicle driver has the right-of-way?
g1-q139.explanation: When changing lanes simultaneously, the driver of the vehicle travelling on the left must yield. The truck is in the left lane and the passenger car is to its right, so the passenger car driver has the right of way (Rules, item 39).

g1-q140.text: Is it permitted to approach the passenger by driving in reverse?
g1-q140.explanation: The image shows sign 5.16 "Bus and (or) Trolleybus Stop". Reversing is prohibited in the places listed in item 50, including on sections of public transport stops, so reversing toward a passenger is prohibited (Rules, items 49, 50, sign 5.16).

g1-q141.text: When entering a yard by making a right turn, we must yield to:
g1-q141.explanation: A courtyard is an adjacent area. When entering an adjacent area from a road, a driver must yield to cyclists and not obstruct pedestrians. Turning right into the courtyard crosses the paths of both the cyclist and the pedestrians walking on the sidewalk, so you yield to both (Rules, item 38).

g1-q142.text: When proceeding uphill in this direction, a U-turn is:
options: Permitted if it can be completed in one maneuver.
Permitted if visibility of 100 m is provided in both directions.
g1-q142.explanation: A U-turn is prohibited where road visibility in at least one direction is less than 100 m, and visibility is limited on an uphill grade. Therefore, a U-turn is permitted only if visibility of at least 100 m is ensured in both directions, while the ability to complete it in a single maneuver does not matter (Rules, item 50, subitem 5).

g1-q143.explanation: The trajectories of the bus and the passenger car intersect in the U-turn zone, and the order of passage is not specified by the Rules, so the driver to whom a vehicle is approaching from the right must yield. The passenger car is approaching the bus from the right, so the bus driver yields (Rules, item 45, sign 6.3.2).

g1-q144.text: A U-turn at this location is:
options: Permitted if visibility is 100 m in both directions.
g1-q144.explanation: Sign 1.22 "Pedestrian Crossing" only warns of a crossing ahead (outside built-up areas it is placed 150–300 m in advance), so the U-turn here is not on the crossing. However, the road curves, and a U-turn is permitted only if visibility is at least 100 m in both directions (Rules, item 50, sign 1.22).

g1-q145.text: Is it permitted to drive across the bridge if doing so does not interfere with the driver of the motorcycle?
g1-q145.explanation: Sign 2.6 "Priority for Oncoming Traffic" prohibits entering a narrow section of road if doing so could impede oncoming traffic, and requires yielding to those approaching the narrow section from the opposite direction. If crossing the bridge does not obstruct the motorcyclist, proceeding is permitted (Rules, sign 2.6).

g1-q146.text: After passing the truck, is it permitted to continue in this lane?
g1-q146.explanation: In the image, out of the two same-direction lanes on a road outside a built-up area, the right lane ahead of the truck is free. Outside built-up areas, occupying left traffic lanes when right lanes are free is prohibited, so after passing the truck it is necessary to change into the right lane (Rules, item 55).

g1-q147.text: In this situation, is it permitted to continue in the occupied lane?
g1-q147.explanation: In the image, the driver is in the left lane of the same direction, while alongside in the right lane a pink truck is driving and ahead there is another truck. Since the right lane is occupied and there is also a need to pass the truck travelling ahead, the driver is permitted to continue driving in the occupied left lane (Rules, item 55).

g2-q1.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a passenger is:
options: A person located in the passenger compartment (cab) of a vehicle or on a vehicle, except the driver and the driving instructor.
A person located in the passenger compartment (cab) of a vehicle or on a vehicle, as well as a person entering or exiting the vehicle, except the driver and the driving instructor.
g2-q1.explanation: According to the Law's definition, a passenger is not only a person inside the cabin (passenger compartment) or on a vehicle, but also a person boarding (getting onto) or alighting (getting off) it—except for the driver and a driving instructor. That is, at the moment of boarding or alighting, a person is already a passenger (Law, art. 2).

g2-q2.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a driver’s license authorizing the operation of category A vehicles may be issued to:
options: Persons who have reached 16 years of age.
Persons who have reached 17 years of age.
Persons who have reached 18 years of age.
g2-q2.explanation: A category "A" driver's license (motorcycles) is issued to persons who have reached 18 years of age. From age 16, only a subcategory "AM" license (mopeds) is issued, and from age 17 one may become a driver candidate, though that is not yet the age for obtaining a license (Law, art. 27, part 3, item 1; art. 28, part 4).

g2-q3.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a driver’s license authorizing the operation of category BE vehicles may be issued to:
options: Persons who have reached 17 years of age.
Persons who have reached 18 years of age.
Persons who have reached 19 years of age.
g2-q3.explanation: A category "BE" driver's license is issued to persons who have reached 19 years of age and already hold a category "B" license. The same age of 19 is also established for categories "CE", "DE" and subcategories "C1E", "D1E", whereas age 18 applies specifically to category "B" (Law, art. 27, part 3, items 1 and 3).

g2-q4.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a roadway is:
options: An element of a road intended for the movement of vehicles.
An element of a road intended for the movement of non-rail vehicles.
g2-q4.explanation: By law, a roadway (carriageway) is an element of a road intended for the movement of trackless vehicles. The law specifies tram tracks as a separate element of the road, so a wording without the clarification "trackless" is incorrect (Law, art. 2).

g2-q5.text: During driving instruction, must the learner driver wear a seat belt?
options: No, if it makes operating the vehicle difficult.
No, if permitted by the driving instructor.
g2-q5.explanation: During driving instruction, the vehicle is driven by the learner, so like any driver, they are required to wear a seat belt. The law allows the driving instructor not to wear a seat belt when the learner is driving, whereas there is no such exception for the learner, even with the instructor's permission (Law, art. 24, part 5, item "b").

g2-q6.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a pedestrian is:
options: A person who is outside a vehicle and on the road, except a person authorized to perform work on the road and performing that work in accordance with the procedure established by law.
A person who is outside a vehicle and on the road, including a person authorized to perform work on the road and performing that work in accordance with the procedure established by law.
g2-q6.explanation: A pedestrian is a person on the road outside a vehicle, except a person authorized to carry out work on the road and performing such work in the manner prescribed by law. That is, persons performing road works are not considered pedestrians, and the wording "including" is incorrect (Law, art. 2).

g2-q7.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, initial practical driving instruction is conducted:
options: On roads outside populated areas, taking into account the intensity of vehicle traffic.
On a closed training area or driving range.
On any road, except freeways, taking into account the intensity of vehicle traffic.
g2-q7.explanation: Initial practical driving training is conducted on a driving range or training ground, and in their absence, in an enclosed area isolated from road traffic. Driving instruction on roads is permitted only accompanied by an instructor, and the learner must know and be able to comply with the requirements of the rules (Law, art. 28, part 7; Rules, items 145–146).

g2-q8.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, is an exit from an adjacent area onto a road considered an intersection?
g2-q8.explanation: The legal definition of "intersection" explicitly states that an exit from an adjacent area (courtyards, parking lots, gas stations, etc.) onto a road is not considered an intersection. When exiting from there, the driver must yield to vehicles moving along the road and not create obstacles for pedestrians (Law, art. 2; Rules, item 38).

g2-q9.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, persons holding a driver’s license for categories B, C, and D may also operate those vehicles with trailers if the trailer’s maximum authorized mass does not exceed:
g2-q9.explanation: Categories "B", "C", "D" (as well as subcategories "C1", "D1") include the respective motor vehicle with a trailer whose maximum authorized mass does not exceed 750 kg. A heavier trailer generally requires a category with "E" ("BE", "CE", "DE"). An exception applies to "B" when the trailer's maximum authorized mass does not exceed the vehicle's unladen mass and the combination's mass does not exceed 3500 kg (Law, art. 27, part 1).

g2-q10.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, bicyclists are prohibited from riding:
g2-q10.explanation: According to the law, when riding a motorcycle, as well as a moped or bicycle on the roadway, the driver must wear a fastened helmet. There is no legal requirement to wear protective goggles, so a cyclist is prohibited from riding only without a helmet (Law, art. 24, part 5, item "c").

g2-q11.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a driver’s license authorizing the operation of category B and C vehicles may be issued to:
options: Persons who have reached 16 years of age.
Persons who have reached 17 years of age.
Persons who have reached 18 years of age.
g2-q11.explanation: A driving license for categories "A", "B", "C" and subcategories "A1", "B1", "C1" is issued to persons who have reached 18 years of age. From age 16, only subcategory "AM" is issued; from age 17, one can become a driver candidate, but the license itself is issued from age 18 (Law, art. 27, part 3, item 1; art. 28, part 4).

g2-q12.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a moped is:
options: A two- or three-wheeled vehicle with an engine displacement not exceeding 50 cm³ and a maximum speed not exceeding 50 km/h.
A two- or three-wheeled vehicle with an engine displacement not exceeding 60 cm³ and a maximum speed not exceeding 60 km/h.
A two- or three-wheeled vehicle with an engine displacement not exceeding 70 cm³ and a maximum speed not exceeding 70 km/h.
g2-q12.explanation: By legal definition, a moped is a two-wheeled or three-wheeled motor vehicle with an engine displacement not exceeding 50 cm³ (or an electric motor of corresponding power) whose maximum design speed does not exceed 50 km/h. The values 60 or 70 do not match the definition: a two-wheeled vehicle with a larger displacement or higher speed is already a motorcycle (Law, art. 2).

g2-q13.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a forced stop is:
options: An interruption of movement caused by the unexpected activation of a prohibitory traffic signal.
An interruption of movement caused by a traffic jam on the road.

Bringing a vehicle to a stationary position because of a vehicle malfunction, the physical and/or mental condition of the driver or passenger, a hazard related to the cargo being transported, or another obstruction that has appeared on the road.
g2-q13.explanation: In the current law, the definition of a forced stop is broad: it includes stopping not only due to a malfunction, the condition of the driver (passenger), cargo, or an obstacle appearing on the road, but also to obey a prohibiting signal of a traffic light or traffic controller, to yield the road, or to prevent a collision with another road user or obstacle (for example, in a traffic jam). Therefore, all listed cases constitute a forced stop (Law, art. 2).

g2-q14.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, insufficient visibility is:
options: The visibility distance of the road during nighttime.
The visibility distance of the road in populated areas when the roadway has no artificial lighting.
Road visibility and/or a visibility distance of up to 300 meters in fog, rain, snowfall, and/or other adverse weather conditions affecting road traffic safety.
g2-q14.explanation: Insufficient visibility means visibility of the road in conditions of fog, rain, snowfall, or other adverse weather and/or a visibility distance of less than 300 meters. The definition is linked to weather conditions, not to dark hours of the day or lack of artificial lighting (Law, art. 2).

g2-q15.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, stopping is:
options: Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for up to 5 minutes, or for the time necessary to pick up or drop off passengers and/or to load or unload the vehicle.
Bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for more than 5 minutes when this is not related to picking up or dropping off passengers or loading or unloading the vehicle.
g2-q15.explanation: Stopping is intentionally bringing a vehicle to a standstill for up to 5 minutes or for as long as necessary for passenger boarding, alighting, and/or loading or unloading. A standstill of more than 5 minutes not related to these actions already constitutes parking (Law, art. 2).

g2-q16.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a public transit vehicle is:
options: A vehicle that operates along a route, has designated stops, and carries passengers and/or baggage, including a tram, trolleybus, or bus.
A vehicle that operates along a route, has designated stops, and carries passengers and/or baggage, including a tram, trolleybus, or bus, as well as a passenger taxi.
g2-q16.explanation: A public transport vehicle is a tram, trolleybus, or bus operating on routes with designated stops and carrying passengers and/or luggage. A taxi is not mentioned in this definition, so it is not considered a public transport vehicle (Law, art. 2).

g2-q17.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the following are considered equivalent to pedestrians:
options: Persons with disabilities moving in non-motorized wheelchairs.
Persons pulling or pushing a handcart, sled, stroller, or wheelchair.
g2-q17.explanation: Equated to pedestrians are persons moving in a non-motorized wheelchair, pulling (pushing) a handcart, sled, stroller, or wheelchair, leading a bicycle, moped, or motorcycle, as well as a person with a disability moving in a motorized wheelchair at pedestrian speed. Therefore, all listed persons are equated to pedestrians (Law, art. 2).

g2-q18.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a trailer (semitrailer) is:
options: Any motor vehicle towed by means of a rigid coupling.
A vehicle not equipped with an engine that is designed to be moved by a motor vehicle and to proceed with it as a single unit, including a special-purpose trailer.
g2-q18.explanation: A trailer (semi-trailer) is a vehicle not equipped with an engine, intended to be set in motion by a motor vehicle and to travel as part of it as a single unit (including a special trailer). A motor vehicle towed by a rigid tow bar is not a trailer, and vehicles coupled together for towing are not considered a road train (Law, art. 2).

g2-q19.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, traffic on the roads of the Republic of Armenia is:
g2-q19.explanation: The law establishes that vehicle traffic on the roads of the Republic of Armenia keeps to the right (right-hand traffic). The same is enshrined in the Road Traffic Rules (Law, art. 7, part 1; Rules, item 2).

g2-q20.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, parking is:
options: Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for more than 5 minutes when this is not related to picking up or dropping off passengers or loading or unloading the vehicle.

Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for more than 5 minutes, except when necessary to prevent a collision with another road user or an obstruction, to pick up or drop off passengers and/or load or unload the vehicle, or in other cases provided by law.
g2-q20.explanation: Parking is intentionally bringing a vehicle to a standstill for more than 5 minutes, except for preventing a collision with another road user or obstacle, passenger boarding or alighting, loading or unloading, and other cases provided by legislation. A wording that omits these exceptions is incomplete (Law, art. 2).

g2-q21.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, persons conscripted into the Armed Forces of the Republic of Armenia or other troops may be issued a driver’s license authorizing the operation of category D and subcategory D1 vehicles upon reaching:
g2-q21.explanation: A driving license of category "D" and subcategory "D1" is generally issued to persons who have reached 21 years of age, and to those conscripted into the Armed Forces and other troops of the RA upon reaching 19 years of age. In both cases, the person must already hold a category "B" or "C" or subcategory "C1" license (Law, art. 27, part 3, item 2).

g2-q22.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, within what period from the date a vehicle is acquired must it be presented for state registration to the registration and examination division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs?
g2-q22.explanation: Ownership rights arising from a transaction involving a vehicle must be submitted for state registration within 15 days from the date of signing the transaction. For an imported vehicle, the same 15 days are counted from the date of customs declaration. The law does not set 10 or 20 days (Law, art. 13, part 2).

g2-q23.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, responsibility for maintaining a vehicle participating in road traffic in technically sound condition is borne by:
options: The owner or user of the vehicle.
The organization that sold the vehicle.
The organization that performed the vehicle’s most recent annual technical inspection.
All of the listed persons and organizations.
g2-q23.explanation: Responsibility for keeping a vehicle in technically sound condition lies with its owner or user. The law places this responsibility neither on the selling organization nor on the organization that conducted the last technical inspection (Law, art. 14, part 2).

g2-q24.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, before starting to drive, the driver must check:
options: The serviceability of the braking system and steering system.
Whether the remaining tire tread depth meets the established standards.
g2-q24.explanation: Before starting to drive (and while driving), the driver is required to check the serviceability of the braking system and steering control, as well as compliance of the tire tread pattern's residual depth with the standards. The same list includes lamps (during dark hours), windshield wipers (during rain or snowfall), and the coupling device, so all listed items are correct (Law, art. 24, part 2, item "a").

g2-q25.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a driver must provide the vehicle for assistance:
options: To police officers for transporting persons in need of urgent medical care to a medical facility.
To medical personnel proceeding in the same direction to provide medical assistance, with the driver’s consent.
g2-q25.explanation: The law obliges the driver to provide the vehicle for assistance both to police officers to transport persons needing urgent medical care to a medical facility, and to medical workers traveling in the same direction to provide medical care (with the driver's consent). Therefore, both cases are correct (Law, art. 24, part 2, item "c").

g2-q26.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, if a driver is involved in a road traffic crash, the driver must:
options: Not move objects related to the crash.
Perform all of the listed actions.
g2-q26.explanation: When involved in a road traffic accident, the driver must immediately stop and not move the vehicle, turn on the hazard warning lights, place the "Emergency Stop" warning triangle, and not move objects related to the accident. Therefore, all listed actions must be performed (Law, art. 24, part 2, item "d").

g2-q27.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the driver of a motor vehicle must carry:
options: A driver’s license authorizing the operation of that category of vehicle and the vehicle registration documents, or, within the Republic of Armenia, their digital versions.
A power of attorney when operating a vehicle belonging to another person.
g2-q27.explanation: The driver of a motor vehicle is required to carry the driving license of the relevant category and the vehicle registration documents (their digital versions are also permitted). A power of attorney is not on this list, so the law does not require it when driving another person's vehicle (Law, art. 24, part 5, item "a").

g2-q28.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a traffic lane is:
options: A marked longitudinal strip of the roadway wide enough for vehicles to proceed in a single line.
A marked or unmarked longitudinal strip of the roadway wide enough for vehicles to proceed in a single line.
g2-q28.explanation: By legal definition, a traffic lane is a marked or unmarked longitudinal strip of a roadway whose width is sufficient for vehicles to move in a single file. That is, a lane exists even where there are no road markings, so a wording mentioning only a marked lane is incomplete (Law, art. 2).

g2-q29.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, maximum authorized mass is:
options: The mass of a fully equipped and fueled vehicle.
The mass of a fully equipped and fueled vehicle, including the driver, passengers and load, established by the manufacturer as the maximum permissible mass.
g2-q29.explanation: Maximum authorized mass is the mass of a fully equipped and fueled vehicle loaded with the driver, passengers, and cargo, established by the manufacturer as the maximum permissible. The mass of only an equipped and fueled vehicle (without people and cargo) is not that (Law, art. 2).

g2-q30.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a traffic controller is:
options: A person authorized to regulate road traffic and carrying out that regulation in accordance with the procedure established by law.
Any road user, including a driver, passenger, or pedestrian, who performs traffic-control actions when necessary.
g2-q30.explanation: A traffic controller is a person authorized to regulate road traffic and performing such regulation in the manner prescribed by legislation. An ordinary road user (driver, passenger, or pedestrian) does not have this authority, so even if they attempt to direct traffic, they are not a traffic controller (Law, art. 2).

g2-q31.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a bicycle is:
options: A vehicle with at least two wheels, normally propelled by the muscular power of a person on it, particularly by means of pedals or hand cranks, as well as a wheelchair.

A vehicle with at least two wheels, normally propelled by the muscular power of a person on it, particularly by means of pedals or hand cranks, excluding a wheelchair; it may also have an electric motor with a maximum continuous rated power not exceeding 0.25 kW that switches off automatically at speeds above 25 km/h.
g2-q31.explanation: By legal definition, a bicycle is a vehicle with at least two wheels that is generally propelled by the muscular power of the person on it using pedals or hand cranks. A wheelchair is not considered a bicycle, so a wording that includes it is incorrect (Law, art. 2).

g2-q32.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a person providing driving instruction:
options: Is considered equivalent to a driver.
Is not considered equivalent to a driver.
g2-q32.explanation: According to the law, a driver is a person operating a vehicle, and a person providing driving instruction (as well as a person driving pack or riding animals or livestock along a road) is also equated to a driver. Therefore, during driving instruction, the instructor is equated to the driver even though the learner is at the wheel (Law, art. 2).

g2-q33.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, an emergency situation is:
options: A situation caused by the action and/or inaction of a road user in which a real danger of a road traffic crash is created.
A situation caused by the action and/or inaction of a road user and/or traffic controller in which a real danger of a road traffic crash is created.
g2-q33.explanation: An emergency situation is a situation arising from an act and/or omission of a road user and/or traffic controller in which a real threat of a road traffic accident is created. The traffic controller is mentioned in the law separately from a road user, so a wording without them is incomplete (Law, art. 2).

g2-q34.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, nighttime is:
options: In fall and winter, the period from 8:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m.; in spring and summer, the period from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.
The period between the end of evening twilight and the beginning of morning twilight.
The period during which sunlight is absent.
g2-q34.explanation: By legal definition, dark hours of the day are the period between the end of evening twilight and the beginning of morning twilight. It is determined by natural lighting, not by fixed hours set according to seasons of the year (Law, art. 2).

g2-q35.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a passenger car is:
options: An automobile with no more than 8 seats intended for passengers and designed and equipped for the safe and comfortable transportation of passengers and baggage.

An automobile with no more than 4 seats intended for passengers, excluding children under 12 years of age, and designed and equipped for the safe and comfortable transportation of passengers and baggage.
g2-q35.explanation: A passenger car is a motor vehicle having no more than 8 passenger seats, intended for the safe and comfortable carriage of passengers and luggage. The law does not provide a 4-seat limit or an exception for children under 12, and a motor vehicle with more than 8 seats is already a bus (Law, art. 2).

g2-q36.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the following are considered equivalent to pedestrians:
options: Persons with disabilities moving at pedestrian speed in motorized wheelchairs.
Persons leading a bicycle, moped, or motorcycle.
g2-q36.explanation: Equated to pedestrians are a person with a disability moving in a motorized wheelchair at pedestrian speed and a person leading a bicycle, moped, or motorcycle, as well as a person moving in a non-motorized wheelchair and a person pulling (pushing) a handcart, sled, stroller, or wheelchair. Therefore, all listed persons are correct (Law, art. 2).

g2-q37.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the right to operate a vehicle arises:
options: Upon successfully passing the practical driving examination at the registration and examination division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
g2-q37.explanation: The right to drive a vehicle arises from the moment of receiving a driving license (or being issued its digital version). Passing the practical exam does not yet grant the right to drive, so driving is not permitted until the license is obtained (Law, art. 27, part 6).

g2-q38.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, international driving permits authorizing the operation of category A and B vehicles may be issued to:
options: Persons who have reached 16 years of age.
Persons who have reached 17 years of age.
Persons who have reached 18 years of age.
g2-q38.explanation: International driving permits for categories "A" and "B" (as well as subcategories "AM", "A1", "B1") are issued to persons who have reached 18 years of age. From age 16, only a national license of subcategory "AM" is issued, and from age 17 one can become a driver candidate (Law, art. 27, part 7).

g2-q39.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, an international driving permit authorizing the operation of category C vehicles may be issued to:
options: Persons who have reached 18 years of age.
Persons who have reached 20 years of age.
Persons who have reached 21 years of age.
g2-q39.explanation: An international driving permit of category "C" is issued to persons who have reached 21 years of age. The same age of 21 is set for international permits of categories "D", "BE", "CE", "DE" and subcategories "C1", "D1", "C1E", "D1E", even though a national category "C" license is issued from age 18 (Law, art. 27, part 7).

g2-q40.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a national driver’s license is issued for:
g2-q40.explanation: A national driving license is issued for a term of ten years. The law does not provide for a lifetime (indefinite) license, while a term of up to three years applies to an international driving permit (Law, art. 27, part 8).

g2-q41.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, an international driving permit is issued for:
g2-q41.explanation: An international driving permit is issued for a term of up to three years, but not exceeding the validity period of the national driving license or the medical clearance certificate. Ten years applies to the national license, and the law does not provide for a lifetime license (Law, art. 27, part 8).

g2-q42.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a person may become a driver candidate, except a candidate for a subcategory AM vehicle, upon reaching:
g2-q42.explanation: According to the law, one can become a driver candidate from age 17, and for subcategory "AM" from age 16. This is not yet the age for receiving a license: licenses for categories "A", "B", "C" are issued from age 18 (Law, art. 28, part 4; art. 27, part 3, item 1).

g2-q43.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, stopping is:
options: Bringing a vehicle to a stationary position in response to a passenger’s request.
Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for more than 5 minutes when this is not related to picking up or dropping off passengers or loading or unloading the vehicle.
Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for up to 5 minutes, or for the time necessary to pick up or drop off passengers and/or to load or unload the vehicle.
g2-q43.explanation: Stopping is intentionally bringing a vehicle to a standstill for up to 5 minutes or for the time necessary for passenger boarding, alighting, and/or loading or unloading. The definition is not limited to a passenger's request, while a standstill exceeding 5 minutes not related to these actions constitutes parking (Law, art. 2).

g2-q44.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the maximum authorized mass of a vehicle is:
options: The maximum mass of a fully equipped and fueled vehicle.
The mass of a fully equipped and fueled vehicle loaded with the driver, passengers, and cargo, established by the manufacturer as the maximum permitted mass.
The mass of a vehicle loaded with the driver, passengers, and cargo, established by the manufacturer as the maximum permitted mass.
g2-q44.explanation: Maximum authorized mass is the mass of a fully equipped and fueled vehicle loaded with the driver, passengers, and cargo, established by the manufacturer as the maximum permissible. Both the load and being equipped and fueled are part of the definition, so wordings omitting either are incomplete (Law, art. 2).

g2-q45.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, persons authorized to operate category B, C, and D vehicles and subcategory C1 and D1 vehicles may also operate them with trailers if the trailer’s maximum authorized mass is:
g2-q45.explanation: Categories "B", "C", "D" and subcategories "C1", "D1" also include the respective motor vehicle with a trailer whose maximum authorized mass does not exceed 750 kg. For a heavier trailer, a category with "E" ("BE", "CE", "DE") is generally required. An exception exists for "B" when the trailer does not exceed the vehicle's unladen mass and the combination does not exceed 3500 kg (Law, art. 27, part 1).

g2-q46.text: When entering a road with an asphalt-concrete surface from an unpaved road, the asphalt-concrete road:
options: Must be considered the priority road.
Must be considered a road of equal priority.
g2-q46.explanation: A road with a hard surface (asphalt concrete, cement concrete, stone materials, etc.) is considered main relative to an unpaved (dirt) road. In the image, we are entering an asphalt-concrete road from a dirt road, so the former is the main road and we must yield (Rules, item 3, subitem 1).

g2-q47.text: How many traffic lanes are there on this roadway?
g2-q47.explanation: A traffic lane is a longitudinal strip of a roadway wide enough for vehicles to travel in a single file. In the image, marking 1.1 divides the roadway into two halves for opposing directions, and one file fits in each half, so there are two lanes. The number of lanes depends on markings and width, not on the number of two-wheeled vehicles traveling side by side (Law, art. 2; Rules, item 51).

g2-q48.text: Under the indicated roadway width, is it permitted to proceed along the center of the roadway?
options: Yes, when there is no oncoming traffic.
g2-q48.explanation: On a two-way road without markings, the left half of the roadway is considered the oncoming traffic side. With a width of 7 m, each direction gets 3.5 m, so driving down the center would partially occupy the oncoming side. Traffic is right-hand, and the absence of oncoming vehicles does not change this (Rules, items 2, 52).

g2-q49.text: Which of the following stationary objects is not considered an obstruction?
options: An automobile stopped because of traffic congestion.
g2-q49.explanation: An obstacle is a stationary object on a lane of the roadway (a damaged or broken-down vehicle, foreign object, road surface damage, etc.) that prevents drivers from continuing along that lane. A car stopped due to a traffic jam is not an obstacle, as it is part of the traffic flow and will move together with the flow (Rules, item 3, subitem 12).

g2-q50.text: Are the sidewalk and shoulders considered part of the road?
g2-q50.explanation: By legal definition, a road includes at least one roadway, and where present, also tram tracks, sidewalks, shoulders, and median strips. Therefore, both the sidewalk and the shoulders are part of the road, not just the shoulder (Law, art. 2).

g2-q51.text: How many roadways does this road have?
g2-q51.explanation: A median strip (divider) is an element of the road separating adjacent roadways and not intended for driving or stopping. In the image, a grass-covered median strip divides the road into two roadways, each having two traffic lanes, so there are four traffic lanes and two roadways (Law, art. 2).

g2-q52.text: How many intersections are shown in this image?
g2-q52.explanation: An intersection is the area where roads intersect, join, or branch at the same level. The intersecting road has a median strip, but it is a single road with two roadways, since a road also includes median strips. Therefore, there is one intersection in the image with two roadway crossings (Law, art. 2).

g2-q53.text: How many intersections of roadways are there at this intersection?
g2-q53.explanation: An area where roads join at the same level is also considered an intersection. The road joining from the right has a median strip, i.e., two roadways, and both join the roadway of our road, so there are two roadway crossings at this intersection (Law, art. 2).

g2-q54.text: How many traffic lanes does this road have?
g2-q54.explanation: The number of traffic lanes is determined by road markings. A grass median strip divides the road into two roadways, and broken line 1.5 divides each of them into two lanes, so the road has four traffic lanes even though there are two roadways (Rules, item 51, marking 1.5).

g2-q55.text: In which image does the road have a median?
g2-q55.explanation: According to the law, a median strip is an element separating adjacent roadways, separated structurally and/or by corresponding road markings. In the left image it is separated only by markings (an area bounded by solid lines), and in the right image structurally (a grass strip), so a median strip is present in both images (Law, art. 2).

g2-q56.text: To yield to other vehicles means that:
options: The driver must not continue or resume driving or perform any maneuver if doing so could force the drivers of other vehicles to change direction or speed.
The driver must not continue or resume driving or perform any maneuver if doing so could force the drivers of other vehicles to unexpectedly change direction or speed.
The driver must stop the vehicle unconditionally.
g2-q56.explanation: By legal definition, "to yield" (give way) means not to continue or resume movement and not to perform a maneuver if doing so could force other drivers to suddenly change their direction of travel or speed. The key word is "suddenly," whereas the definition does not require unconditionally stopping the vehicle (Law, art. 2).

g2-q57.text: In which image is an intersection shown?
g2-q57.explanation: An intersection is the area where roads intersect, join, or branch at the same level, whereas an exit from an adjacent area is not considered an intersection. In the left image, another road joins the road, which is an intersection. In the right image, no other road joins the street, and exits from courtyards are exits from an adjacent area (Law, art. 2).

g2-q58.text: How many intersections of roadways are there at the intersection?
g2-q58.explanation: A median strip separates adjacent roadways of a road. The intersecting road has such a strip, meaning two roadways, and the roadway of our road crosses each of them, so at this single intersection there are two roadway crossings (Law, art. 2).

options: Leaving the traffic lane occupied by the vehicle while maintaining the original direction of movement.
Leaving the row occupied by the vehicle within a marked traffic lane while maintaining the original direction of movement.
g2-q59.explanation: Lane changing (repositioning) is when a vehicle, while maintaining its initial direction of travel, exits the traffic lane it occupies or the file it occupies within a marked traffic lane. The definition covers both cases, so neither wording alone is complete (Rules, item 3, subitem 7).

options: A maneuver performed for the purpose of entering another road.
A maneuver performed for the purpose of entering another road or an adjacent area from the road.
g2-q60.explanation: A turn is a vehicle maneuver performed to exit onto another road or from a road onto an adjacent area. Therefore, turning off a road into a courtyard, parking lot, or gas station is also a turn, and a wording mentioning only exiting onto another road is incomplete (Rules, item 3, subitem 9; Law, art. 2).

options: Driving a vehicle in the opposite direction.
A maneuver performed for the purpose of changing the vehicle’s direction of movement to the opposite direction.
g2-q61.explanation: A U-turn is a maneuver performed to change a vehicle's direction of travel to the opposite (oncoming) direction. Simply driving in the oncoming direction is not a U-turn, since the essence of the definition is the maneuver of changing direction (Rules, item 3, subitem 10).

g2-q62.text: Passing without leaving the lane means:
options: Proceeding ahead of one or more moving vehicles without leaving the occupied lane.
Proceeding ahead of one or more moving vehicles by leaving the occupied lane.
g2-q62.explanation: Passing (advancing ahead) is moving faster than one or more moving vehicles without leaving the occupied lane. If moving ahead involves leaving the occupied lane, it is already overtaking (Rules, item 3, subitems 11, 14).

options: The moment a vehicle begins moving from a stopping or parking location, with or without changing to an adjacent traffic lane.
The moment a vehicle begins moving from a stopping or parking location while changing to an adjacent traffic lane.
g2-q63.explanation: Starting movement is the moment a vehicle begins moving from a stopping or parking place, whether associated with changing into an adjacent traffic lane or without it. That is, starting to move counts as starting movement even when the driver does not merge into an adjacent lane (Rules, item 3, subitem 5).

options: Starting to move a vehicle (involving entry into an adjacent traffic lane), changing lanes, changing direction, stopping (with a lane change), and backing.
Starting to move a vehicle, changing lanes, changing direction, stopping, and backing.
g2-q64.explanation: Maneuvering includes starting movement (associated with moving into an adjacent traffic lane), lane changing, changing direction of travel, stopping (while changing lanes/repositioning), and reversing. The clarifications in parentheses are important: starting movement without moving into an adjacent lane or stopping without lane changing are not maneuvers (Rules, item 3, subitem 6).

g2-q65.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a truck is:
options: An automobile designed by its construction and equipment for the transportation of cargo.
An automobile weighing more than 3.5 metric tons and designed by its construction and equipment for the transportation of cargo.
g2-q65.explanation: By legal definition, a truck (goods vehicle) is a motor vehicle designed by its construction and equipment to carry cargo; mass is not part of the definition. The 3500 kg threshold separates driving license categories, not the concept of a truck (Law, art. 2; art. 27, part 1).

g2-q66.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a median is:
options: A structurally separated road element that divides adjacent roadways and is not intended for vehicle or pedestrian traffic or stopping.
A road element that divides adjacent roadways, is separated structurally and/or by appropriate pavement markings, and is not intended for vehicle or pedestrian traffic or stopping.
g2-q66.explanation: According to the law, a median strip is an element of a road separating adjacent roadways, separated structurally and/or by corresponding markings, and not intended for driving or stopping. Therefore, a strip separated only by markings is also a median strip, and a wording that omits markings is incomplete (Law, art. 2).

g2-q67.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a vehicle is:
options: A device designed to transport a person, cargo, or equipment installed on it along a road.
g2-q67.explanation: By legal definition, a vehicle is a device intended for transporting people, cargo, or equipment mounted on it along a road. A car and a motorcycle are merely examples of it, not the complete definition (Law, art. 2).

g2-q68.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the following persons are considered equivalent to drivers:
options: A person driving pack and/or riding animals or livestock along a road.
A person driving pack and/or riding animals or livestock.
g2-q68.explanation: Equated to a driver are a person providing driving instruction, as well as a person driving pack and/or riding animals or livestock along a road. The decisive clarification is the phrase "along a road": only a person driving animals along a road is equated to a driver (Law, art. 2).

g2-q69.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the following are considered equivalent to motorcycles:
options: Three-wheeled motor vehicles with a mass of up to 400 kg in fully equipped and fueled condition, excluding the driver, cargo, and passengers.
Quadricycles with a motorcycle-type seating position or motorcycle-type handlebars.
g2-q69.explanation: According to the law, quadricycles with a motorcycle-style saddle or motorcycle-type handlebars, as well as tricycles, are equated to a motorcycle, but only if their mass does not exceed 400 kg and their power does not exceed 15 kW. A wording about three-wheeled vehicles limited only by mass is incomplete, while all-terrain ATVs (quadrocycles) are not equated to motorcycles (Law, art. 2).

g2-q70.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a sidewalk is:
options: A road element adjacent to the roadway and intended for pedestrian movement in accordance with the procedure established by law.
A road element separated from the roadway in any manner and intended for pedestrian movement in accordance with the procedure established by law.
g2-q70.explanation: By legal definition, a sidewalk is an element of a road intended for pedestrian movement, adjacent to the roadway or separated from it in some way. The definition covers both cases, so both wordings are correct (Law, art. 2).

g2-q71.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, an automobile is:
options: A motor vehicle designed for transporting people or cargo on a road, or for towing a vehicle used to transport cargo, excluding vehicles such as agricultural tractors for which transporting people or cargo on a road, or towing a vehicle used to transport cargo, is only an additional function.

A motor vehicle designed for transporting people or cargo on a road, or for towing a vehicle used to transport cargo, including vehicles such as agricultural tractors for which transporting people or cargo on a road, or towing a vehicle used to transport cargo, is only an additional function.
g2-q71.explanation: By legal definition, a motor car (automobile) is a motor vehicle intended for carrying people or cargo along a road or towing a vehicle carrying cargo. The definition does not include vehicles such as agricultural tractors, for which this is an auxiliary function, so a wording that classifies tractors as automobiles is incorrect (Law, art. 2).

g2-q72.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a national driver’s license of the Republic of Armenia authorizing the operation of Category “A” vehicles also authorizes the operation of:
options: Vehicles of subcategory “B1” having a motorcycle-type seat or handlebar.
g2-q72.explanation: A category "A" driving license also grants the right to drive vehicles of subcategories "AM", "A1", and subcategory "B1" vehicles equipped with a motorcycle-style seat or handlebars. That is, all listed vehicles are permitted with this license (Law, art. 27, part 10).

g2-q73.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a national driver’s license of the Republic of Armenia authorizing the operation of Category “B” vehicles also authorizes the operation of:
options: Vehicles of subcategory “B1,” except vehicles having a motorcycle-type seat or handlebar.
g2-q73.explanation: A category "B" driving license also grants the right to drive vehicles of subcategory "B1", except those with a motorcycle-style seat or handlebars. Subcategory "AM" is not on that list, so driving a moped with a category "B" license is not permitted (Law, art. 27, part 10).

g2-q74.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, international driving permits issued by the competent authorities of the Republic of Armenia are considered, for purposes of driving vehicles within the territory of the Republic of Armenia:
g2-q74.explanation: According to the law, international driving permits issued by competent authorities of the RA are considered invalid for driving vehicles within the territory of the RA. To drive in Armenia, one must hold a national driving license (Law, art. 27, part 5, item 1).

g2-q75.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the right to drive vehicles arises:
options: Upon receipt of the driver’s license.
Upon assignment of the digital version of the driver’s license.
g2-q75.explanation: The right to drive vehicles arises from the moment of receiving a driving license or being issued its digital version, so both cases are correct. Merely passing the exam does not yet grant the right to drive (Law, art. 27, part 6).

g2-q76.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, driver’s licenses obtained in other countries by citizens of the Republic of Armenia, including dual citizens, that comply with the requirements for driver’s licenses under the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic and its subsequent amendments and supplements are considered valid within the territory of the Republic of Armenia, from the date those persons enter the Republic of Armenia, for:
g2-q76.explanation: Driving licenses obtained in other countries by RA citizens (including dual citizens) that comply with the Vienna Convention are valid in Armenia for three months from the moment of entry into the country. The law does not specify a period of one year or six months (Law, art. 27, part 5, item 2).

g2-q77.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, persons applying for a driver’s license for the first time to operate vehicles of which of the following categories must submit to the registration and examination division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs a certificate confirming that they have undergone medical certification?
g2-q77.explanation: A certificate of having passed medical clearance must be submitted by applicants applying for the first time for a license of categories "C", "D", "T" (and related other categories and subcategories). For category "B", applicants are referred for clearance only in specific cases, so lists containing "B" are incorrect (Law, art. 28, parts 1.6 and 1.3).

g2-q78.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, if a driver candidate undergoing practical driving instruction violates the traffic rules, liability in accordance with the law is borne by:
options: The driving instructor of the training center or the person providing individual practical driving instruction.
g2-q78.explanation: For a violation of rules during practical driving instruction, responsibility lies not with the learner, but with the driving instructor of the training center or the person providing individual driving instruction. The law equates the person teaching driving to the driver (Law, art. 28, part 9; art. 2).

g2-q79.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, when may an 18- year-old who holds a national driver’s license for Categories “B” and “C” obtain an international driving permit for the same categories?
options: At the same time as the national driver’s license is obtained.
g2-q79.explanation: An international driving permit is issued from age 18 for categories "A" and "B", and only from age 21 for categories "C" and "D". A national category "C" license can be obtained from age 18, but an international permit for categories "BC" only after reaching age 21 (Law, art. 27, part 7).

g2-q80.text: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, when may a 19- year-old who holds a national driver’s license for Categories “BE” and “CE” obtain an international driving permit for the same categories?
options: At the same time as the national driver’s license is obtained.
g2-q80.explanation: An international driving permit for categories "C", "D", "BE", "CE", "DE" is issued to persons who have reached age 21 (and for "A", "B" from age 18).
