This marking prohibits stopping along its entire length, and dropping off a passenger is not exempted from it. A solid yellow line at the curb is not applied randomly: it appears where even a single car stopping creates a real problem—in front of shop and building entrances, on narrow street sections, or near an intersection and crosswalk where visibility must stay open. From this very behind-the-wheel view, you can see that the buildings come straight to the sidewalk and the street is not wide: a car stopped at this spot both narrows the flow and hides a pedestrian stepping out between cars from everyone else. Key point: a marking does not need a sign to take effect. Even if there is not a single sign in the scene, the yellow line on the ground establishes the ban on its own, and the driver must check the line's color and continuity before pulling up to the curb. The exam trap is treating "it's just to drop off a passenger" as sufficient justification. Stop duration does not matter: the stopping location decides. • Dropping off a passenger seems brief, and that brevity is tempting, yet a solid yellow line at the curb makes no exceptions based on stop duration. • Climbing onto the sidewalk not only fails to solve the problem, it adds a second violation to the first: the sidewalk is pedestrian territory, and occupying it is prohibited.

g7-q49.text: Is it permitted to continue in the direction indicated by the arrow?
options: Permitted for the purpose of stopping to drop off passengers.
Permitted for the purpose of passing the truck.
g7-q49.explanation: Only for a brief stop to pick up or drop off passengers. The right traffic lane in the image is marked with the letter "A" on the roadway: this lane is dedicated to route vehicles. The line separating it from your lane is dashed, not solid, and that single detail decides the entire question's answer. When a dedicated lane's boundary is dashed, entry by other cars is not banned absolutely, but restricted: you may enter it to turn right, to enter or exit a road, and for a brief stop near the roadway edge to pick up or drop off passengers—provided you do not obstruct route vehicles. If that same boundary were solid, entry would be prohibited under all circumstances. The traffic and safety logic is plain: the whole point of a dedicated lane is for buses to bypass queues and stay on schedule. If private cars were allowed to pass using it or travel long stretches in it, the rationale for the dedicated lane would collapse—and worse, a private car and a bus running in the same lane at different speeds would create rear-end collision risks. Yet stopping for a few seconds at the right edge does not disrupt the bus flow. Rule to remember: check the marking type of the dedicated lane's boundary. Dashed means "entry permitted for specific purposes," solid means "entry prohibited." • "Prohibited" is the answer for a dedicated lane separated by a solid marking: in this image the boundary is dashed, meaning the ban is not absolute. • "Permitted in all cases" destroys the meaning of a dedicated lane: ordinary sustained driving by a private car in a bus lane is not permitted. • Passing a truck using the dedicated lane is the exact thing the law seeks to prevent: entry for specific purposes is permitted only for turning, entering/exiting, and picking up or dropping off passengers.

g7-q50.text: This type of vertical pavement marking indicates:
options: The lower edges of a bridge or tunnel.
The entrance to an unlit tunnel.
Any element of a road structure that creates a hazard for traffic.
g7-q50.explanation: Vertical marking 2.2 with vertical black and white stripes marks the lower edges of a bridge, overpass, and tunnel to make their clearance dimensions visible. Hazardous lateral elements of road structures are marked with marking 2.1.1–2.1.3 using diagonal stripes. (Rules, item 171, marking 2.2)

g7-q51.text: What should the passenger-car driver do if the bus driver has begun braking?
options: Reduce speed, stop if necessary, and continue after making sure there are no pedestrians in the crossing.
Stop and continue only after the bus resumes driving.
g7-q51.explanation: Reduce your speed, stop if necessary, and proceed only after making sure there are no pedestrians on the crossing. In the picture, the bus in the left lane is braking: its brake lights are on, and just ahead on the roadway, the yellow marking of a pedestrian crossing is visible. The passenger car is in the adjacent lane and slightly behind, i.e., in the exact position where the tall body of the bus blocks its view of the crossing. The rule is straightforward: if a vehicle in an adjacent lane has slowed down or stopped before a pedestrian crossing, drivers in other lanes moving in the same direction may continue only after making sure there are no pedestrians on the crossing. The bus braking is a warning, not an obstacle: you should read it as "a pedestrian is likely crossing," not as "my path is clear." The safety reason behind this rule is one of the most well-known urban crash scenarios: a pedestrian steps out from behind a stopped vehicle, neither side sees the other until the last moment, and impact occurs at full speed. A pedestrian hidden behind a bus simply does not exist to you until the moment of collision. Key takeaway: wherever a vehicle in an adjacent lane slows down near a crossing, your visibility is incomplete. Slow down so you can stop before the crossing line, and only then, once you see the crossing is clear, continue driving. • Continuing at the same speed is tempting because your lane appears empty; however, you cannot see why the bus is braking, and this exact blind spot hides a pedestrian on the crossing from you. • Waiting until the bus moves on is more than required: the law does not require stopping to wait for the bus to resume moving, the bus may remain at a stop for several minutes, and an unnecessary stop creates a risk of a rear-end collision.

g7-q52.text: The bus driver has stopped to pick up passengers. The passenger car is proceeding at a speed of 70 km/h. Which vehicle driver is violating the requirements of the traffic rules?
g7-q52.explanation: The "GYUMRI" sign on a blue background (5.25) indicates that rules for driving outside built-up areas apply, where the maximum permissible speed for passenger cars is 90 km/h (70 km/h is not a violation). Within the zone of sign 2.1 "Priority road," the bus has stopped on the shoulder (rather than parking on the roadway), so no one is violating the rules (Rules, items 69, 78, 86, sign 5.25).

g7-q53.text: Where must the driver stop in this situation?
options: Before the intersection of the traffic lanes.
g7-q53.explanation: Before the "Stop line" marking. When a stop line is applied on the roadway, it is what determines the stopping point—not an approximate estimate of the distance to the traffic light and not the edge of the intersection. In the picture, the transverse white line is visible right before the yellow pedestrian crossing marking, and the traffic light is installed on the right: the driver must stop so that the front bumper does not cross this line. The stop line's position is calculated: far enough back so that a stopped car does not encroach on the pedestrian crossing and pedestrians' path stays open, and far enough forward so that the driver can see the traffic light and cross traffic. If you stop past the line, you push pedestrians off their path and force them to weave between cars; if you stop much earlier, you reduce intersection throughput and sometimes miss traffic light sensors. Remember the order of priority: the stop line; in its absence, a sign or traffic light; and in the absence of both, the edge of the intersecting roadway in a position that gives you full visibility. A common trap in this question is the "before the traffic light" option. A traffic light is usually placed higher and further forward than the stop line, and if you drive up to its base, you will effectively stop on the pedestrian crossing. • Both the traffic light and the stop line are visible in the picture: ignoring them and passing a controlled intersection without stopping is unacceptable. • The traffic light is placed further forward than the stop line: stopping at its base means stopping on the pedestrian crossing marking. • The edge of the intersection is a reference only when there is neither a stop line nor a sign; here the stop line is applied, and it takes priority.

g7-q54.text: The bus has stopped to yield to a pedestrian. In this situation, is the passenger-car driver violating the requirements of the traffic rules?
g7-q54.explanation: Yes, the passenger car driver is violating the rules. In the picture, the bus has stopped before a pedestrian crossing—with a crossing sign to the right of the roadway marking—to yield to pedestrians, while the red car drives past it and approaches the crossing. Two rules are violated at once. First, when a vehicle in an adjacent lane has stopped before a crossing, other drivers may proceed only after making sure there are no pedestrians; in practice, this means you must stop and look. Second, going around and passing on a pedestrian crossing are prohibited. The safety reason speaks more clearly than the rule itself: the tall body of the bus acts like a wall. A pedestrian crossing in front of the bus does not see the red car, and the red car's driver does not see the pedestrian: they spot each other when the distance is only a few meters and the car's speed has not changed. This scenario is one of the deadliest urban crashes. Key takeaway: treat any vehicle stopped before a crossing as a warning, not an obstacle. Its message is: "someone is crossing whom you cannot see." • The temptation is that the red car's driver does not see any pedestrian and the road ahead looks clear; yet this very "not seeing" is the reason for the prohibition, because their view is blocked by the body of the bus.

g7-q55.text: Where must the bus driver stop in order to yield to the passenger car before continuing to the left?
options: At a safe location at the driver’s discretion.
g7-q55.explanation: At the road marking. Two things are visible at once in the picture: on the right, the triangular "Yield" sign, and on the roadway, a row of white triangles. This marking shows the exact place where you must stop, if necessary, to yield the right of way. This means the bus driver must move forward to the marking and stop there, not at the sign. The reason is sightline geometry. The sign is usually placed further back and at the edge of the road: from that point, visibility of the priority road is insufficient, and if you stop there, you will both needlessly block traffic behind you and be forced to creep forward blindly to see oncoming traffic. The triangular marking is applied at the closest possible point to the intersecting roadway so that you have visibility while your vehicle's body stays outside the passenger car's path. For a long bus wanting to turn left, these few meters are the difference between a safe turn and a side impact. Remember the general rule: if a stopping-location marking exists, that is the stopping place; if there is no marking, it is the edge of the intersecting road's roadway. The exam trap is the option that leaves the decision to the driver's discretion: in priority rules, the stopping place is never a matter of discretion. • The sign is a warning location, not a stopping location: stopping at the sign neither provides sufficient visibility of the priority road nor complies with the place defined by the marking. • "A safe place at the driver's discretion" replaces the rule with personal judgment: when a marking is applied on the roadway, the stopping location is defined, leaving no choice.

g7-q56.text: Where must the driver stop in this situation?
g7-q56.explanation: Before the "Stop line" marking. Two signs are visible in the picture: the triangular "Yield" sign with a "STOP 250m" plaque, which only announces that a "Stop" sign is 250 meters ahead, and the red octagonal "STOP" sign installed right at the intersection. The arrow near the curb shows the same 250-meter distance. The first sign does not require stopping: its job is to prepare the driver to slow down and not be caught by surprise. The mandatory stop belongs to the "Stop" sign, but its exact position is determined by the marking: since a stop line is applied on the roadway, you must stop before this line, not level with the sign post. Order to remember: if a stop line is applied, it is the reference; if there isn't one, stop before the "Stop" sign and at a spot from which you have a full view of the intersecting road. The stop line's position is chosen so that a stopped car does not enter the path of traffic on the priority road, while the driver can see both directions. A common trap is confusing the advance sign with the "250 m" plaque for the "Stop" sign itself and stopping hundreds of meters early, blocking traffic behind you. • The first sign is only a warning and with the "250 m" plaque states that the stop is further ahead; stopping at its base is neither necessary nor safe. • Stopping level with the "Stop" sign is almost right, but when a stop line is applied, it is the exact reference for stopping. • The "Stop" sign makes a full stop mandatory: driving through without stopping is a violation even if the intersecting road appears empty.

g7-q57.text: Which vehicles are permitted to stop within the area where this sign is in effect?
options: Only vehicles driven by persons with disabilities.
Only taxis with the taximeter activated.
Stopping is prohibited for all vehicles.
g7-q57.explanation: Sign 3.27 "No stopping" is installed in the picture. Unlike sign 3.28 ("No parking"), sign 3.27 makes no exception for vehicles driven by persons with disabilities or taxis, and stopping of public transit vehicles is prohibited outside designated stops, so stopping in the sign's zone is prohibited for everyone (Rules, item 85, sign 3.27).

g7-q58.text: Within the area where these traffic signs are in effect, is stopping to pick up passengers permitted?
g7-q58.explanation: Sign 3.28 "No parking" is installed with plaque 8.2.2 "Zone of effect" (200 m). This sign prohibits only parking of vehicles and does not prohibit stopping, so stopping to pick up passengers is permitted (Rules, sign 3.28, 8.2.2).

g7-q59.text: For which vehicles is the lane marked with the letter “A” designated?
options: Only buses operating on an established route.
g7-q59.explanation: Marking 1.23.1 in the form of the letter "A" painted on the right lane of the roadway designates a dedicated lane intended for all public transit vehicles (buses, trolleybuses, and minibuses operating on an established route). It is not intended only for buses or taxis (Rules, item 124, marking 1.23.1).

g7-q60.text: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
g7-q60.explanation: Warning sign 1.11.1 "Dangerous curve" is installed on the right side of the road. According to the rules, near dangerous curves (with visibility under 100 m), stopping is prohibited only on the roadway, whereas in the picture the car has stopped off the roadway—on the shoulder—which is permitted (Rules, items 78, 84, sub-item 5).

g7-q61.text: Is parking permitted in this situation?
g7-q61.explanation: The picture shows a road outside a built-up area marked with sign 2.1 "Priority road," and the car is parked on the roadway. Outside built-up areas, parking on the roadway of roads marked with sign 2.1 "Priority road" is prohibited regardless of the time of day (Rules, item 86, sub-item 2).

g7-q62.text: At which of the indicated locations is stopping permitted?
g7-q62.explanation: Stopping is prohibited on pedestrian crossings and closer than 5 m before them in the direction of travel. Position A is 3 m before the crossing in our direction, and position C is on the opposite side of a two-way road directly before the crossing in that direction (less than 5 m). Only position B is located after the crossing, so stopping is permitted only at location B (Rules, item 84, sub-item 4).

g7-q63.text: At which location is stopping permitted?
g7-q63.explanation: Sign 5.5 establishes one-way traffic, which allows stopping on the left side as well in a built-up area (position A), since the effect of sign 3.27 "No stopping" installed on the right applies only to the right side of the road. Plaque 8.2.3 (with a downward arrow) placed under sign 3.27 indicates the end of the prohibition zone, so stopping is prohibited at position C and permitted at position B after the sign (Rules, item 79, sign 3.27, 8.2.3).

g7-q64.text: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
options: Only for the purpose of picking up a passenger.
g7-q64.explanation: On the left side of the road, there is sign 5.16 "Bus and/or trolleybus stop" and marking 1.17. Under the rules, stopping is prohibited closer than 15 m from public transit stops marked with marking 1.17, including for the purpose of picking up a passenger (Rules, item 84, sub-item 7).

g7-q65.text: In the indicated situation, is stopping permitted for the purpose of picking up a passenger?
g7-q65.explanation: In the picture, the car is about to stop inside a tunnel. Under the rules, stopping in tunnels is prohibited for any purpose, including picking up or dropping off passengers (Rules, item 84, sub-item 2).

g7-q66.text: In which of the indicated cases is stopping permitted?
g7-q66.explanation: One-way traffic is established on the road by sign 5.5, so stopping on the left side is permitted in a built-up area. However, positions A and C are located directly before the pedestrian crossing in the direction of travel (closer than 5 m), where stopping is prohibited, whereas position B is after the crossing, so stopping is permitted only in case B (Rules, items 79, 84, sub-item 4).

options: At a railroad crossing and within 50 m of it.
At a railroad crossing and within 50 m before it.
g7-q67.explanation: Stopping is prohibited directly on the railway crossing itself. Meanwhile, within 50 m of a crossing, only parking is prohibited, not stopping. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 2; item 86, sub-item 3)

options: At a railroad crossing and within 50 m of it.
At a railroad crossing and within 50 m before it.
g7-q68.explanation: Parking is prohibited both in places where stopping is prohibited (including on a railway crossing) and closer than 50 m to railway crossings—on both sides of the crossing (and not only before the crossing). (Rules, item 86, sub-items 1, 3)

g7-q69.text: Which option shows a vehicle stopped correctly?
g7-q69.explanation: The picture shows a two-way road with shoulders outside a built-up area. Outside built-up areas, stopping is permitted only on the right side of the road—on the shoulder (stopping on the roadway is allowed only if there is no shoulder). A stopped on the left side and B stopped on the roadway, so only driver C stopped properly (Rules, items 78, 79).

g7-q70.text: Must you yield to the truck?
g7-q70.explanation: A car with its hazard warning lights on is stopped in the oncoming lane, creating an obstacle for the oncoming truck. When oncoming traffic passage is obstructed (on level conditions without slope signs), the driver who has the obstacle on their side must yield, so we are not required to yield to the truck (Rules, item 46).

g7-q71.text: Stopping at the indicated location is:
g7-q71.explanation: The car has stopped past the pedestrian crossing in the direction of travel, so the 5 m prohibition before the crossing is not violated. At the same time, the distance between the stopped car and the solid line is 3 m (not less than 3 m), and the distance from the edge of the intersecting roadway is 5 m (not less than 5 m); therefore, stopping is permitted (Rules, item 84, sub-items 3, 4, 6).

g7-q72.text: When is it permitted to cross the pavement marking?
g7-q72.explanation: In the picture, there is a pedestrian crossing ahead marked with signs 5.19.1 and 5.19.2 and zebra stripes, and our car is about to overtake the cyclist and the truck on the left. Since overtaking on pedestrian crossings is prohibited, crossing the broken line is permitted only after the pedestrian crossing (Rules, item 77, sub-item 2).

g7-q73.text: Has the truck driver violated the stopping rules?
g7-q73.explanation: The truck has stopped at the right edge of the roadway, and the width from solid marking 1.1 shown in the picture to the edge is only 3 m. Since the space remaining between the stopped vehicle and the solid marking is less than 3 m, stopping at this location is prohibited, and the driver has violated the rules. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 3)

g7-q74.text: In the indicated situation, is stopping permitted for the purpose of picking up a passenger?
options: Permitted only for the driver of a public transit vehicle.
g7-q74.explanation: Sign 5.16 ("Bus and/or trolleybus stop") is installed on the right in the picture. Closer than 15 m from public transit stops (signposts), stopping is prohibited for all other drivers, including to pick up or drop off passengers, so only the driver of a public transit vehicle may stop there. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 7, item 85)

g7-q75.text: Which driver has violated the parking rules?
options: Only the driver of the motorcycle.
g7-q75.explanation: In the middle of the roadway is double solid marking 1.3, from which the width to the right curb is 3 m. The passenger car is parked at the right edge less than 3 m from the solid marking, thereby violating the parking rules, whereas the motorcycle is in motion and not parked. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 3, item 86, sub-item 1)

g7-q76.text: Which option shows a driver parked in a prohibited position?
g7-q76.explanation: In the absence of a roadway widening or another arrangement permitted by plaques 8.6.2–8.6.9 and markings, a vehicle must be parked parallel to the edge of the roadway in a single row. Car B is parked properly—parallel to the edge—while car A is positioned at an angle to the edge, which is prohibited. (Rules, item 80)

g7-q77.text: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
options: Only for the purpose of dropping off a passenger.
g7-q77.explanation: The car's intended stopping place is directly before a pedestrian crossing equipped with signs 5.19.1, 5.19.2 and marking 1.14.1, as well as closer than 15 m to a public transit stop. Stopping closer than 5 m before a pedestrian crossing in the direction of travel is prohibited in all cases, regardless of the purpose of dropping off a passenger. (Rules, item 84, sub-items 4 and 7)

g7-q78.text: At which of the indicated locations is parking permitted?
g7-q78.explanation: With sign 5.5 ("One-way road") installed on the right, parking in a built-up area is permitted on both the right and left sides of the road. The effect of sign 3.28 ("No parking") applies only to the side of the road on which it is installed (on the right—to location B beyond the sign), so parking is permitted at locations A (on the left side) or C (before the sign). (Rules, item 79, sub-item 2, sign 3.28)

g7-q79.text: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
g7-q79.explanation: The picture shows an intersection with sign 4.3 ("Roundabout"), and the indicated stopping spot is directly within the intersection boundaries—on the circular roadway. Stopping is prohibited at intersections, at roadway junctions, and closer than 5 m from the edge of the intersecting roadway, so stopping is not permitted in this case. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 6)

g7-q80.text: Who has violated the stopping rules?
g7-q80.explanation: At the three-way intersection, the passenger car is stopped 5 m from the edge of the intersecting roadway (the rule prohibits less than 5 m), and to its left is broken marking 1.5, so the rules are not violated. Although the truck is 10 m from the intersection, its lane is bounded on the left by solid marking 1.1, with less than 3 m between the marking and the truck, so only the truck driver has violated the stopping rules. (Rules, item 84, sub-items 3 and 6)

g7-q81.text: In which case has the driver violated the stopping rules?
options: Both drivers have violated the rules.
g7-q81.explanation: The picture shows a railway crossing with a barrier, equipped with signs 1.1 and 1.4.3, and cars A and B have stopped on the shoulders outside the crossing (A at a distance of 40 m). Under the rules, within 50 m of a railway crossing only parking is prohibited, whereas stopping is prohibited only directly on the crossing itself, so no one has violated the stopping rules. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 2, item 86, sub-item 3)

g7-q82.text: In which case has the driver violated the parking rules?
options: Both drivers have violated the rules.
g7-q82.explanation: On both sides of the railway crossing, car A (40 m from the crossing) and car B (even closer to the crossing) are parked on the shoulders. Since parking closer than 50 m to railway crossings is prohibited in both directions from the crossing, both drivers have violated the parking rules. (Rules, item 86, sub-item 3)

g7-q83.text: Is parking permitted at the indicated location?
g7-q83.explanation: Sign 5.27 ("Parking restriction zone") (with the inscription "ZONE" and the image of sign 3.28) is installed on the right. Unlike the regular sign 3.28, the zone sign applies across the entire width of the road—to both the right and left sides up to sign 5.28—so parking on the left side is also prohibited. (Rules, sign 5.27)

g7-q84.text: Is stopping on the bridge permitted for the purpose of picking up a passenger?
g7-q84.explanation: In the picture, the driver is about to stop on a bridge to pick up a passenger. Under the Road Traffic Rules of the Republic of Armenia, stopping on bridges, overpasses, and viaducts is strictly prohibited regardless of the number of lanes or the purpose of the stop. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 2)

g7-q85.text: Which driver has violated the stopping rules?
g7-q85.explanation: On a road outside a built-up area, the car driver stopped on the left shoulder (on the oncoming side), which is permitted only inside built-up areas. The motorcycle rider stopped directly on the roadway without using the free right shoulder, so both drivers violated the stopping rules. (Rules, items 78, 79)

g7-q86.explanation: This road has sign 5.26 ("End of built-up area") on a blue background, in whose zone (both before and after the sign) the rules governing traffic in built-up areas do not apply. Consequently, stopping on the left side of the road—at locations A and B—is prohibited, and only driver C stopped properly on the right shoulder. (Rules, items 78, 79, sign 5.26)

g7-q87.text: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
g7-q87.explanation: On a road with a median strip and no shoulder, the width of the right lane is 4 m, and on the left it is separated by solid marking 1.1. Since a passenger car is about 1.8–2 m wide, stopping there would leave less than 3 m between the car and the solid line, so stopping at this location is prohibited. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 3)

g7-q88.text: Which driver has violated the parking rules?
g7-q88.explanation: Sign 6.4 ("Parking area") installed with plaque 8.6.3 specifies the parking method: parallel to the curb with the right wheels partially on the sidewalk. The red car is positioned this way, whereas the passenger car is parked perpendicular to the curb, violating the parking arrangement required by the plaque. (Rules, item 81, sign 6.4, plaque 8.6.3)

g7-q89.text: Is the driver of a truck weighing less than 3.5 metric tons permitted to park in the manner indicated on the supplemental plaque?
g7-q89.explanation: Sign 6.4 ("Parking area") with plaque 8.6.3 allows parking alongside the curb partially on the sidewalk. However, under the rules, parking by the method specified by plaques 8.6.2, 8.6.3, 8.6.6–8.6.9 is permitted only for passenger cars, motorcycles, mopeds, and bicycles, so it is prohibited even for a truck weighing under 3.5 tons. (Rules, item 81)

g7-q90.text: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
g7-q90.explanation: The stopping spot indicated by the white arrow is located immediately past the intersection—less than 5 m from the edge of the intersecting roadway. Since stopping closer than 5 m to the edge of an intersecting roadway is prohibited, stopping at the indicated location is not permitted. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 6)

g7-q91.text: At which of the indicated locations is stopping permitted?
g7-q91.explanation: Sign 3.27 ("No stopping") is installed in the picture with plaque 8.2.3 ("Zone of effect") bearing a downward arrow, indicating the end of the no-stopping zone. Car A is stopped past the sign on the right shoulder, where the prohibition does not apply, whereas car B, although also past the sign, stopped on the roadway without using the shoulder; therefore, stopping is permitted only at location A. (Rules, item 78, plaque 8.2.3)

g7-q92.text: Parking at the indicated location is:
g7-q92.explanation: Sign 5.16 ("Bus and/or trolleybus stop") is installed on the right side of the road with a median strip. Since the intended parking spot is located 15 m away from the stop sign (not less than 15 m), parking at this location is permitted. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 7, item 86, sub-item 1)

g7-q93.text: Which driver has violated the parking rules?
g7-q93.explanation: Sign 6.4 ("Parking area") with plaque 8.6.6 specifies a particular parking method: perpendicular to the edge of the roadway with the front wheels on the sidewalk. Car A is parked in accordance with the plaque, whereas car B is parked parallel to the curb on the roadway, thereby violating the parking rules. (Rules, item 81, plaque 8.6.6)

g7-q94.text: Stopping at the indicated location is:
options: Permitted for the purpose of picking up a passenger.
g7-q94.explanation: The car has stopped before a pedestrian crossing marked with signs 5.19.1 and 5.19.2 and marking 1.14.1, while solid marking 1.1 runs along the center of the roadway. Stopping closer than 5 m before a pedestrian crossing (in the picture, the 5 m measurement reaches the car's front wheel, so the front part is closer than 5 m to the crossing), as well as less than 3 m from a solid line, is prohibited in all cases regardless of the purpose of picking up a passenger. (Rules, item 84, sub-items 3 and 4)

g7-q95.text: Which driver has violated the stopping rules?
g7-q95.explanation: Solid marking 1.2 indicating the edge of the roadway is painted along the right edge of the road, with a shoulder to its right. Car A has pulled completely onto the shoulder, whereas cars B and C stopped partially on the roadway, violating the requirement to stop on the shoulder. (Rules, item 78)

g7-q96.text: Are the drivers permitted to stop at the indicated location?
options: Only the driver of the motorcycle.
g7-q96.explanation: Sign 4.1.1 ("Proceed straight") is installed on the road, and the width from solid marking 1.1 of the roadway to the right curb is only 3 m. Under such conditions, if any vehicle (whether a car or a motorcycle) stops, the distance from it to the solid marking will be less than 3 m, so stopping is prohibited for both. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 3)

g7-q97.text: In which of the indicated cases is stopping permitted?
g7-q97.explanation: Sign 5.23.1 ("Start of built-up area") on a white background is installed at the start of the road, beyond which built-up area traffic rules apply. Since this is a road with one lane in each direction (with broken marking 1.5) and no tram tracks in the middle, stopping is permitted on both the right side (C) and the left side—on the shoulder or at the edge of the roadway (A and B). (Rules, item 78, item 79, sub-item 1)

g7-q98.text: Is stopping in this position permitted?
g7-q98.explanation: The red car has stopped perpendicular to the right edge of the roadway without a local roadway widening or corresponding marking and plaque. The rules require vehicles to be positioned parallel to the edge of the roadway in a single row, so stopping in such a position is prohibited for everyone. (Rules, item 80)

g7-q99.text: Stopping at the indicated location is:
options: Permitted if the distance from the vehicle to the pavement marking is more than 3 meters.
g7-q99.explanation: Sign 2.1 ("Priority road") is installed, and the car intends to stop opposite the non-continuing side of a three-way intersection. However, on the opposite side it is separated by combined marking 1.11 rather than a solid line or median strip, so the three-way intersection exception does not apply, and stopping is prohibited even when the distance is more than 3 m. (Rules, item 84, sub-item 6)

options: Approach to a curved section of road.
Approach to the end of the lane.
g7-q100.explanation: Horizontal marking 1.19 painted on the asphalt as curved arrows warns drivers that they are approaching the end of a lane (road narrowing) and need to merge into the adjacent lane. It does not grant priority when changing lanes and does not indicate a curved section. (Rules, marking 1.19)

g7-q101.text: What does this pavement marking indicate?
options: Approach to the “Stop Line” at a signal-controlled intersection.
Approach to the “Stop Line” pavement marking when it is used together with a “STOP” sign.
g7-q101.explanation: Horizontal marking 1.21 in the form of the word "STOP" on the roadway warns of approaching marking 1.12 ("Stop line") when used in conjunction with sign 2.5 ("Stop"). It is not used to warn of approaching a controlled intersection or a barrier. (Rules, marking 1.21)

options: Movement along a dangerous section of road.
g7-q102.explanation: Black-and-white vertical marking 2.5 on the side surface of metal roadside guardrails serves as a visual guidance aid and indicates driving along a dangerous section of road. It is not associated with a railway crossing or an intersection. (Rules, item 171, marking 2.5)

options: Approach to a location where drivers must yield.
Approach to a location where vehicles must stop.
g7-q103.explanation: The large triangular horizontal marking 1.20 painted on the traffic lane warns of approaching marking 1.13 (the place where you must yield). It does not indicate a dangerous curve or a mandatory stopping point. (Rules, marking 1.20)

g7-q104.text: These broken pavement markings within the intersection indicate:
g7-q104.explanation: Broken marking 1.7 with short dashes used within the boundaries of an intersection marks traffic lanes inside the intersection itself, helping drivers stay in their lane. Permitted directions of travel are shown by arrows 1.18, not marking 1.7. (Rules, marking 1.7)

g7-q105.text: With this pavement marking, passing is:
g7-q105.explanation: To the left of the tractor is marking 1.11, with its broken line on the driver's side (right) and its solid line on the oncoming side. Since marking 1.11 may be crossed from the side of the broken line, overtaking is permitted in this case. (Rules, marking 1.11)

options: Marks all vertical elements adjacent to the roadway.
Marks only those elements of road structures that present a hazard to drivers.
g7-q106.explanation: Vertical marking 2.1.1–2.1.3 with slanted black-and-white stripes painted on overpass piers marks only those elements of road structures that pose a hazard to moving vehicles. Not all vertical elements adjacent to the roadway are marked with this marking. (Rules, item 171, marking 2.1.1–2.1.3)

g7-q107.text: With this pavement marking, may you enter the intersection if doing so does not interfere with the passenger-car driver?
g7-q107.explanation: Sign 2.4 ("Yield") is installed and marking 1.13 (a row of triangles) is painted in the picture, a passenger car is approaching from the right on the priority road, and visibility to the left is limited. The driver must yield to all vehicles traveling on the intersecting road and, if necessary, stop before marking 1.13 without entering the intersection. (Rules, item 96, marking 1.13)

g7-q108.text: Which driver following the indicated path does not violate the pavement-marking requirements?
g7-q108.explanation: The broken side of marking 1.11 separating opposing traffic flows is on the side of the pink car (B), while the solid side is on the side of the silver car (A) emerging from the oncoming direction. Since marking 1.11 may be crossed only from the side of the broken line, only the driver making a U-turn along path B complies with the marking, whereas A crosses it from the solid-line side. (Rules, marking 1.11)

g7-q109.text: In which case is it permitted to cross the solid pavement marking?
g7-q109.explanation: Solid marking 1.2 indicates the edge of the roadway. On the right side (B), the marking separates the roadway from the shoulder and may be crossed when stopping, whereas on the left side (A) it separates the median strip, where stopping and crossing the line are prohibited. (Rules, item 78, marking 1.2)

g7-q110.text: What does the broken pavement marking indicate?
options: The right to stop on the shoulder.
The edges of the roadway on a two-lane road.
The right to proceed on the shoulder.
g7-q110.explanation: The broken white marking running along both edges of a two-lane road indicates the edges of the roadway. It does not permit driving on the shoulder (which is prohibited by item 61), but merely separates the roadway from the shoulder. (Rules, item 61, marking 1.2)

g7-q111.text: In this situation, proceeding along this path is:
g7-q111.explanation: The center lane is bounded on both sides by double broken marking 1.9, and the signals of the reversible-lane traffic lights above it are turned off. According to the rules, if the signals of a reversible-lane traffic light above a lane marked on both sides with marking 1.9 are off, entering that lane is strictly prohibited. (Rules, item 13)

g7-q112.text: Is parking permitted at the indicated location?
options: Permitted without driving onto the sidewalk.
g7-q112.explanation: Yellow solid marking 1.4 is painted along the right edge of the roadway (curb). Marking 1.4 prohibits both stopping and parking on that side of the road, so parking at this location is prohibited. (Rules, item 170, marking 1.4)

g7-q113.text: With this pavement marking, passing is:
options: Permitted if the vehicle ahead is a slow-moving vehicle.
g7-q113.explanation: To the left of the tractor is marking 1.11, with its solid line on the driver's side (right) and its broken line on the oncoming side. Since crossing marking 1.11 from the solid-line side is prohibited, overtaking is prohibited even when the vehicle ahead is slow-moving. (Rules, marking 1.11)

g7-q114.text: May you continue beyond the sign?
g7-q114.explanation: On the right in the direction of travel, sign 2.5 ("Stop") is installed, and ahead—before the intersection—marking 1.12 ("Stop line") is painted. The driver may pass the sign and continue to marking 1.12 "Stop line," before which they must make a mandatory stop. (Rules, sign 2.5, marking 1.12)

g7-q115.text: When orange and white pavement markings conflict, drivers:
options: May follow whichever pavement marking is more convenient.
Must follow the white pavement marking.
Must follow the orange pavement marking.
g7-q115.explanation: Horizontal markings are permanent (white, and in certain cases yellow and red) or temporary (orange). When the requirements of temporary and permanent markings conflict with each other, drivers must follow the requirements of the temporary orange marking. (Rules, items 170, 174)

g7-q116.text: Which driver is permitted to cross the solid pavement marking when stopping?
options: The driver proceeding from the opposite direction.
g7-q116.explanation: The solid marking to the right of the oncoming car indicates the edge of the roadway (1.2), which may be crossed to stop on the shoulder. Meanwhile, to the right of our lane is a channelizing island (1.16.2/1.16.3) bounded by solid line 1.1, onto which driving and stopping are prohibited, so only the driver coming from the oncoming direction may cross the line. (Rules, item 78, markings 1.2, 1.16)

g7-q117.text: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
g7-q117.explanation: Yellow broken marking 1.10 is painted on the right curb of the roadway. Marking 1.10 prohibits only parking of vehicles, but does not prohibit stopping, so stopping at the indicated location is permitted. (Rules, item 170, marking 1.10)

options: Indicates the boundaries of a Residential Zone.
g7-q118.explanation: Horizontal marking 1.25 consisting of staggered white squares in a checkerboard pattern across the roadway indicates a speed bump for forced speed reduction. It does not mark the boundaries of a residential zone and does not prohibit traffic. (Rules, marking 1.25)

options: Traffic to the left of it or over it.
g7-q119.explanation: Broken marking 1.5 painted down the center of the road separates traffic flows of opposite directions on a two-lane road. This marking permits overtaking, bypassing, and U-turns, but prohibits driving to the left of it (in the oncoming lane) or directly on it. (Rules, item 60, marking 1.5)

options: The maximum permitted speed on the indicated road section.
g7-q120.explanation: Horizontal marking 1.24.2 showing "50" inside a circle on the traffic lane duplicates prohibitory sign 3.24 and indicates the maximum permissible speed on that section of road. A route number is indicated by an alphanumeric inscription, while a recommended speed is shown inside a square. (Rules, marking 1.24.2)

g7-q121.text: The marking applied to the roadway indicates:
options: The distance from the nearest intersection.
The distance from the nearest populated area.
g7-q121.explanation: Horizontal marking 1.24.3 reading "A 100" on the roadway indicates the number of that road or route. It does not indicate the distance to the nearest intersection or built-up area. (Rules, marking 1.24.3)

g7-q122.text: On which side may the obstruction be passed?
g7-q122.explanation: At a roadwork section (1.25), mandatory sign 4.2.2 ("Pass obstacle on the left") is mounted on the obstacle. Although solid marking 1.1 runs on the left, the sign's requirement takes precedence over the marking, so the obstacle may be bypassed only in direction A—on the left. (Rules, sign 4.2.2)

g7-q123.text: Which vehicles may use the rightmost lane of this road?
g7-q123.explanation: Above the rightmost lane of the road, sign 5.14 ("Lane for public transit vehicles") is installed and marking 1.23 with the letter "A" is painted. Only public transit vehicles (trolleybuses and public transit buses), and not just any bus, are permitted to drive in this lane. (Rules, item 124, sign 5.14)

g7-q124.text: Is parking permitted at the indicated location?
g7-q124.explanation: Yellow broken marking 1.10 is painted on the right curb of the roadway. Within the zone of marking 1.10, parking of vehicles is prohibited (except for taxis or vehicles of persons with disabilities in cases provided for by the rules), so parking here is prohibited. (Rules, item 170, marking 1.10)

g7-q125.text: The increasing length of the broken pavement-marking segments indicates:
options: Approach to the end of the lane.
Approach to a dangerous road section.
That the pavement marking will soon become a solid line.
g7-q125.explanation: An increase in the length of the dashes of a broken marking (approach line 1.6) warns the driver that the broken marking separating traffic flows is soon transitioning into a solid line (1.1 or 1.11). It does not indicate the end of a lane or a dangerous section. (Rules, marking 1.6)

g7-q126.text: In the indicated situation, proceeding straight ahead is:
options: Permitted after changing to the right lane.
g7-q126.explanation: The car is in the left lane, on which arrow 1.18 permits turning left only (or making a U-turn). Since the dividing line with the adjacent right lane is still broken (1.5), the driver may go straight after first changing into the right lane. (Rules, item 60, marking 1.18)

g7-q127.text: How many traffic lanes does this road have?
g7-q127.explanation: Double solid marking 1.3 is painted in the center of the road, and two traffic lanes are marked on each side by broken marking 1.5. Therefore, the road has a total of four traffic lanes—two in each direction. (Rules, item 51, markings 1.3, 1.5)

g8-q1.text: What is the maximum permitted speed for passenger cars on roads outside populated areas?
g8-q1.explanation: On roads outside built-up areas, the maximum speed for passenger cars is 90 km/h (except on motorways, where up to 110 km/h is permitted). Therefore, the options 100 km/h, 80 km/h, and 70 km/h are incorrect. (Rules, item 69, sub-item 1)

g8-q2.text: Trucks carrying people in an equipped cargo bed are permitted to proceed at a speed not exceeding:
g8-q2.explanation: Trucks carrying people in an equipped cargo bed are permitted to travel at a speed of no more than 60 km/h regardless of the road type. Speeds of 70 and 80 km/h exceed the permissible limit. (Rules, item 71, sub-item 1)

g8-q3.text: Vehicles transporting organized groups of children are permitted to proceed at a speed not exceeding:
g8-q3.explanation: The speed of vehicles carrying organized groups of children must not exceed 60 km/h. Driving at 70 or 80 km/h during such transport is prohibited. (Rules, item 71, sub-item 1)

g8-q4.text: In populated areas, vehicles are permitted to proceed at a speed not exceeding:
g8-q4.explanation: In built-up areas, all vehicles are permitted to travel at a speed of no more than 60 km/h (unless another speed is set by sign 3.24, and up to 20 km/h in residential zones). 80 km/h is the maximum limit that can be set only by a special sign, while 90 km/h applies outside built-up areas. (Rules, items 68, 70)

g8-q5.text: At what speed are trucks with a maximum authorized mass not exceeding 3.5 metric tons permitted to proceed outside populated areas?
g8-q5.explanation: Outside built-up areas, trucks with a permissible maximum weight of no more than 3.5 t are permitted to travel at a speed of no more than 90 km/h (just like passenger cars). The 70 km/h limit applies to trucks weighing more than 3.5 t. (Rules, item 69, sub-items 1, 3)

g8-q6.text: During towing, if the hazard warning lights are absent or malfunctioning, the emergency warning triangle must be placed:
options: At the rear of the towed vehicle.
At the front of the towing vehicle.
On either vehicle, in a visible location, at the driver’s discretion.
g8-q6.explanation: During towing, if the hazard warning lights are absent or malfunctioning, the "Warning triangle" (emergency stop sign) is mounted on the rear of the towed vehicle to warn drivers approaching from behind. Placing it at the front or elsewhere at the driver's discretion does not comply with the rules. (Rules, item 24)

g8-q7.text: When towing with a rigid coupling, the distance between the vehicles must not exceed:
g8-q7.explanation: When towing with a rigid coupling (tow bar), the distance between the towing and towed vehicles must not exceed 4 m. Meanwhile, a distance of 4–6 m applies to towing with a flexible coupling (tow rope). (Rules, item 140)

g8-q8.text: When towing with a rigid or flexible coupling, is it permitted to carry people in the cargo bed of a truck?
options: Permitted in the cargo beds of both the towing and towed trucks.
Permitted only in the cargo bed of the towed truck.
Permitted only in the cargo bed of the towing truck.
Prohibited in the cargo beds of both trucks.
g8-q8.explanation: When towing with a rigid or flexible coupling, carrying people in the cargo bed of the towed truck is prohibited. Therefore, carrying people in the cargo bed of a truck is permitted only in the bed of the towing vehicle. (Rules, item 139)

g8-q9.text: When towing with a rigid or flexible coupling, in which of the following cases is carrying people in the towed vehicle permitted?
options: In the cargo bed of a truck when towing with a rigid coupling.
g8-q9.explanation: When towing with a rigid or flexible coupling, carrying people in a towed bus, trolleybus, or in the cargo bed of a truck is prohibited. In such a case, carrying passengers in a towed vehicle is permitted only in a passenger car (as well as in a truck's cab). (Rules, item 139)

g8-q10.text: What is the maximum permitted speed when towing with a motor vehicle?
g8-q10.explanation: When towing motor vehicles, the maximum permissible speed is 50 km/h. The options 30 and 40 km/h are unnecessarily low, while 60 and 70 km/h exceed the established limit. (Rules, item 71, sub-item 2)

g8-q11.text: Under icy road conditions, towing is prohibited:
g8-q11.explanation: In icy conditions, towing with a flexible coupling is prohibited because on a slippery road the towed vehicle may collide with the towing vehicle or skid. Towing with a rigid coupling or by partial loading is permitted in icy conditions. (Rules, item 143, sub-item 3)

g8-q12.text: What is the maximum speed at which towing may be performed under the indicated conditions?
g8-q12.explanation: The picture shows a motor vehicle being towed with a flexible coupling, and sign 3.24 ("Maximum speed limit" — 80 km/h) is installed. Although the sign allows up to 80 km/h on this road, the maximum speed during towing may in no case exceed 50 km/h. (Rules, item 71, sub-item 2, item 72)

g8-q13.text: When towing with a flexible or rigid coupling, is carrying people in the towed motor vehicle permitted?
options: Permitted in a bus and trolleybus.
Permitted only in a passenger car.
Permitted in the cargo bed of a truck and in a passenger car.
Permitted in the cab of a truck and in a passenger car.
g8-q13.explanation: When towing with a flexible or rigid coupling, carrying people in a towed bus, trolleybus, or in the cargo bed of a truck is prohibited. Therefore, carrying people in a towed vehicle is permitted only in the cab of a truck and in a passenger car. (Rules, item 139)

options: Is permitted when towing with a rigid coupling or by the partial-loading method.
g8-q14.explanation: In icy conditions, only towing with a flexible coupling is prohibited. Towing with a rigid coupling or by partial loading is permitted, as these methods ensure safe steering and braking. (Rules, item 143, sub-item 3)

g8-q15.text: What is the maximum permitted speed when towing a vehicle with a flexible coupling?
g8-q15.explanation: When towing with a flexible coupling, the maximum speed is 50 km/h (as with all types of towing). Driving at a higher speed (60 or 70 km/h) is prohibited. (Rules, item 71, sub-item 2)

g8-q16.text: In which case is towing prohibited?
options: Under icy road conditions with a rigid coupling.
Under icy road conditions with a flexible coupling.
g8-q16.explanation: In icy conditions, towing with a flexible coupling is prohibited. Towing with a rigid coupling and towing by/of motorcycles with a sidecar are permitted in icy conditions (only towing by or of motorcycles without a sidecar is prohibited). (Rules, item 143, sub-items 2, 3)

g8-q17.text: When towing motor vehicles outside populated areas, the speed must not exceed:
g8-q17.explanation: When towing motor vehicles—both inside and outside built-up areas—the speed must not exceed 50 km/h. Therefore, speeds of 60 and 70 km/h are prohibited. (Rules, item 71, sub-item 2)

options: Towing motorcycles with sidecars is permitted.
Towing motorcycles without sidecars is permitted.
g8-q18.explanation: Under the rules, towing by motorcycles without a sidecar and towing of such motorcycles are prohibited. Therefore, towing is permitted only for motorcycles with a sidecar. (Rules, item 143, sub-item 2)

g8-q19.text: When towing, what distance between the vehicles must be maintained by a flexible coupling?
g8-q19.explanation: When towing with a flexible coupling, the distance between the towing and towed vehicles must be within 4–6 m. A shorter distance increases the risk of collision, while more than 6 m increases the risk of the tow rope snapping or other cars cutting in (up to 4 m is for a rigid coupling). (Rules, item 140)

g8-q20.text: What is the maximum permitted speed on freeways for passenger cars towing a trailer?
g8-q20.explanation: Passenger cars with a trailer are permitted to travel on motorways at a speed of no more than 90 km/h (and 70 km/h on regular non-urban roads). Speeds of 100 km/h and 110 km/h apply to passenger cars without a trailer. (Rules, item 69, sub-item 3)

g8-q21.text: When towing with a rigid coupling, the distance between the vehicles must not exceed:
g8-q21.explanation: When towing with a rigid coupling, the distance between the vehicles must not exceed 4 m. The 5 m and 6 m options belong to the permissible range for a flexible coupling (4–6 m). (Rules, item 140)

g8-q22.text: When towing a motor vehicle by the partial-loading method, carrying passengers is permitted:
options: In the cargo bed of the towing vehicle.
In the cab of the towed vehicle.
In the cargo bed of the towed vehicle.
In the cab of the towing vehicle.
g8-q22.explanation: When towing by partial loading, people are prohibited from being in either the cab or cargo bed of the towed vehicle, as well as in the cargo bed of the towing vehicle. Therefore, carrying passengers is permitted only in the cab of the towing vehicle. (Rules, item 139)

g8-q23.text: Is towing motorcycles with sidecars permitted?
options: Permitted only with a rigid coupling.
g8-q23.explanation: Since only towing by motorcycles without a sidecar and towing of such motorcycles are prohibited, towing motorcycles with a sidecar is permitted without being restricted solely to a rigid coupling. (Rules, item 143, sub-item 2)

g8-q24.text: What is the maximum permitted speed when towing with a flexible coupling?
g8-q24.explanation: When towing with a flexible coupling, the maximum speed is 50 km/h. Speeds of 60 km/h and 70 km/h exceed the permissible limit. (Rules, item 71, sub-item 2)

g8-q25.text: Cargo must be positioned and, when necessary, secured on the vehicle so that it:
options: Does not extend above the sides of the cargo bed.
Does not create significant noise, raise dust, or pollute the road or the environment.
Does not extend more than 0.8 m beyond the rear edge of the vehicle.
g8-q25.explanation: The load must be placed and secured so that it does not make significant noise, raise dust, or pollute the road and environment. There is no ban on stacking above the sideboards (total height is limited to 4 m), and the permissible rear overhang without marking is 1 m, not 0.8 m. (Rules, item 162, item 163, item 164, sub-item 4)

g8-q26.text: Children may be carried in the front seat of a passenger car that is not equipped with a child restraint system if they have reached the age of:
g8-q26.explanation: Carrying children under 12 years of age in the front seat of a passenger car is permitted only with the use of child restraint systems (devices) appropriate for the child's weight and height. Without such a device, children may be carried in the front seat only after reaching 12 years of age. (Rules, items 159, 159.1)

g8-q27.text: Is carrying people in a cargo trailer permitted?
options: Permitted only for persons accompanying the cargo.
g8-q27.explanation: Carrying people in a cargo trailer is strictly prohibited in all cases, regardless of whether they are accompanying persons or not. (Rules, item 158, sub-item 1)

g8-q28.text: Is carrying children under 12 years of age on the rear seat of a motorcycle permitted?
g8-q28.explanation: Carrying children under 12 years of age on the rear seat of a motorcycle is prohibited for safety reasons. (Rules, item 159.3)

g8-q29.text: While the vehicle is moving, are persons permitted to be in the cargo bed of a truck if it is not equipped for carrying people?
options: Permitted on roads that are not freeways.
Permitted only for persons accompanying the cargo or proceeding to receive it, provided they are seated on seats installed below the level of the sides of the cargo bed.
g8-q29.explanation: In the cargo bed of flatbed trucks not equipped for carrying people, only persons accompanying the cargo or traveling to receive it are permitted to ride, provided they are supplied with seats secured below the upper edge of the sideboards (at least 0.3 m lower and 0.3–0.5 m above the floor). (Rules, items 153, 154)

g8-q30.text: Carrying people in a cargo trailer is:
options: Permitted only for persons accompanying the cargo.
g8-q30.explanation: Carrying people in a cargo trailer is prohibited in all cases, including carrying persons accompanying the cargo. (Rules, item 158, sub-item 1)

g8-q31.text: When towing with a flexible or rigid coupling, is carrying people in the towed motor vehicle permitted?
options: Permitted in a bus and trolleybus.
Permitted in the cab of a truck and in a passenger car.
Permitted in the cargo bed of a truck and in a passenger car.
g8-q31.explanation: When towing with a flexible or rigid coupling, carrying people in a towed vehicle is permitted only in the cab of a truck and in a passenger car. People are prohibited from being in a towed bus, trolleybus, or in the cargo bed of a truck. (Rules, item 139)

g8-q32.text: What is the maximum speed permitted for a motorcycle in areas designated by the “Residential Zone” and “End of Residential Zone” signs?
g8-q32.explanation: In areas marked with the "Residential zone" and "End of residential zone" signs (as well as in courtyard areas), vehicles, including motorcycles, are permitted to travel at a speed of no more than 20 km/h. Speeds of 30 and 40 km/h exceed the permissible limit. (Rules, item 68)

g8-q33.text: When carrying people in an equipped cargo bed, the truck driver must proceed at a speed not exceeding:
g8-q33.explanation: When carrying people in an equipped cargo bed, the truck driver must drive at a speed of no more than 60 km/h. 70 km/h exceeds the limit, while 50 km/h applies to towing. (Rules, item 71, sub-item 1)

g8-q34.text: During towing, the towed vehicle must have the following activated:
g8-q34.explanation: During towing, the hazard warning lights must be turned on on the towed vehicle to warn other road users of the hazard. Low-beam headlights during the day are turned on on the towing vehicle. (Rules, item 22, sub-item 4; item 133, sub-item 6)

g8-q35.text: What is the maximum permitted speed for vehicles within areas where the “Residential Zone” and “End of Residential Zone” traffic signs apply?
g8-q35.explanation: Within the zone of the "Residential zone" and "End of residential zone" signs, vehicles are permitted to travel at a speed of no more than 20 km/h. There are no 5 km/h or 10 km/h limits in the rules. (Rules, item 68)

g8-q36.text: What is the maximum permitted speed for the driver of a truck with a maximum authorized mass not exceeding 3.5 metric tons within the area of effect of these signs?
g8-q36.explanation: Sign 3.24 ("Maximum speed limit" — 50 km/h) installed outside a built-up area is combined with plaque 8.4.1, which applies only to trucks with a permissible maximum weight over 3.5 tons. Consequently, the 50 km/h limit does not apply to a truck weighing no more than 3.5 tons, and it may travel at up to 90 km/h as established for that vehicle outside built-up areas. (Rules, item 69, sub-item 1, plaque 8.4.1)

g8-q37.text: When towing a motor vehicle, in which lane may you continue on this road?
g8-q37.explanation: Sign 5.15.3 ("Start of lane") is installed on the right, showing sign 4.6 ("Minimum speed limit" — 60 km/h) for the main lane. Since speed when towing a motor vehicle cannot exceed 50 km/h, the driver cannot maintain at least 60 km/h and must continue driving only in the right additional lane. (Rules, item 71, sub-item 2, sign 5.15.3)

g8-q38.text: What conditions must a driver take into account when selecting a speed within the permitted limits?
options: The condition of the road surface.
Visibility in the direction of movement.
g8-q38.explanation: When choosing a speed within the permitted limits, the driver must take into account traffic intensity, the condition of the vehicle and cargo, as well as the condition of the road surface and visibility in the direction of travel. Therefore, both stated conditions must be taken into account. (Rules, item 65)

g8-q39.text: Within the permitted limits, what maximum speed should a driver select?
options: A speed that ensures full control of the vehicle.
The driver may select any speed that does not exceed the maximum permitted speed.
g8-q39.explanation: Within permissible limits, the driver must choose a speed that makes it possible to maintain full control of the vehicle. Choosing any speed not exceeding the maximum permissible limit is unacceptable if it does not match the road conditions. (Rules, item 66)

options: Exceeding the maximum speed specified by the technical characteristics of the vehicle.
Exceeding the speed specified by the “Speed Limit” identification sign displayed on the vehicle.
Driving at an unnecessarily low speed and thereby impeding the movement of other vehicles.
Braking suddenly unless necessary to prevent a traffic accident.
g8-q40.explanation: A driver is prohibited from exceeding the speed specified by the vehicle's technical specifications or the "Speed limit" identification sign, driving unnecessarily at a very low speed and obstructing others, as well as braking abruptly unless required to prevent a traffic accident. Therefore, all of the listed actions are prohibited. (Rules, item 72)

g8-q41.explanation: The picture shows signs 2.4 ("Yield" — 1), 5.21 ("Residential zone" — 2), 6.2 ("Recommended speed" — 3), and 1.18 ("Loose gravel" — 4). Of these signs, only sign 5.21 ("Residential zone") imposes a mandatory speed limit—a maximum of 20 km/h—whereas 6.2 only indicates a recommended (preferred) speed. (Rules, item 68, sign 5.21)

options: Crossing a railroad crossing at a speed greater than 30 km/h.
Crossing a railroad crossing at a speed below 30 km/h.
Proceeding across a railroad crossing, without the permission of the head of the railroad track section, in slow-moving vehicles with a speed below 8 km/h or in tractors coupled to sledges.
g8-q42.explanation: Without permission from the head of the railway track section, crossing a level crossing with slow-moving machines at speeds below 8 km/h and tractors towing harrows/sleds is prohibited. The rules do not set a 30 km/h speed threshold for crossing a railway crossing. (Rules, item 114, sub-item 4)

g8-q43.text: When approaching an intersection, the driver must operate the vehicle at a speed that:
options: Does not exceed the maximum permitted speed established for that road section.
Allows the driver to stop and yield to vehicles having the right-of-way.
g8-q43.explanation: When approaching an intersection, the driver must drive at a speed that allows them to stop and let pass (yield to) vehicles that have the right of way. Simply not exceeding the maximum permissible speed is not enough. (Rules, item 86.1)

g8-q44.text: A driver is prohibited from increasing speed:
options: If doing so would prevent a driver who is passing from completing the passing maneuver.
If doing so is necessary to clear the way for a driver who has stopped in order to yield.
If doing so is necessary to clear the intersection.
g8-q44.explanation: The driver of a vehicle being overtaken is prohibited from preventing the overtaking driver from completing the maneuver by increasing speed or by any other actions. However, increasing speed to clear the road for a driver who stopped to yield, or to clear an intersection, is not prohibited. (Rules, item 75)

options: When approaching a vehicle displaying the “Transportation of Children” identification sign while children are boarding or exiting.
When an obstruction or danger to traffic arises.

When approaching a vehicle displaying flashing blue and red beacons and using a special audible signal, as well as when approaching a stationary vehicle displaying flashing blue or flashing blue and red beacons.
In all of the above cases.
g8-q45.explanation: The driver must reduce speed when approaching a vehicle bearing the "Children transport" sign while children are boarding or alighting, when dazzled, when an obstacle or hazard arises, as well as when a vehicle with blue and red flashing beacons and an audible signal approaches or when approaching a stopped vehicle with a flashing beacon. Therefore, speed must be reduced in all of the listed cases. (Rules, items 29, 30, 67, 129, 156)

g8-q46.text: If cargo protrudes 0.5 m beyond the side of the vehicle, measured from the outer edge of the marker light, must it be marked during daylight hours with the “Oversized Cargo” identification sign and, at night or under conditions of insufficient visibility, additionally with a white light or reflector at the front and a red light or reflector at the rear?
g8-q46.explanation: Yes, if the cargo protrudes laterally beyond the outer edge of the vehicle's position light by more than 0.4 m (0.5 m > 0.4 m), then during daylight hours it must be marked with the "Oversized load" identification sign, and in the dark and in conditions of insufficient visibility, also with white lights or reflectors at the front and red ones at the rear. (Rules, item 162)

g8-q47.text: A truck whose driver holds a driver’s license for Categories B and C, and which meets the requirements for transporting people in a truck, may carry up to:
g8-q47.explanation: Vehicles of category "C" (trucks), when conditions for carrying people are met, are permitted to carry up to 8 passengers. To carry more than 8 passengers, one must also hold a category "D" or "DE" or subcategory "D1" or "D1E" driving license. (Rules, item 150)

g8-q48.text: It is prohibited to transport children under 12 years of age:
options: In the cargo bed of a truck with sideboards.
In the enclosed cargo body of a truck.
g8-q48.explanation: Carrying children under 12 years of age in the cargo bed of a flatbed truck is prohibited. Carrying children under 12 years of age in the body of a box (van-body) truck is permitted. (Rules, item 159.3)

g8-q49.text: If cargo protrudes 1.2 m beyond the rear end of the vehicle, must it be marked during daylight hours with the “Oversized Cargo” identification sign and, at night or under conditions of insufficient visibility, additionally with a white light or reflector at the front and a red light or reflector at the rear?
g8-q49.explanation: Yes, cargo protruding beyond the front or rear dimensions of the vehicle by more than 1 m (1.2 m > 1 m) must be marked during daylight hours with the "Oversized load" identification sign, and in the dark and in conditions of insufficient visibility, also with white lights or a reflector at the front and red ones at the rear. (Rules, item 162)

g8-q50.text: Transportation of cargo is prohibited if the cargo:
options: Restricts the driver’s field of vision.
Makes the vehicle difficult to control or reduces its stability.
Obscures exterior lights or reflectors, license plates, or identification signs, or prevents hand signals from being seen.
In all of the above cases.
g8-q50.explanation: Carrying cargo is prohibited if it restricts the driver's visibility, hinders steering and impairs stability, or covers external lighting devices, reflectors, license plates, identification signs, and interferes with the perception of hand signals. Therefore, the prohibition applies in all of the specified cases. (Rules, item 164, sub-items 1–3)

g8-q51.text: If the condition or placement of the cargo does not allow it to be transported in compliance with the rules, the driver must:
options: Deliver the cargo safely to the nearest unloading location.
Correct the violations or stop proceeding.
g8-q51.explanation: If the condition and placement of the cargo do not meet the requirements of the rules, the driver must take measures to eliminate the violations or cease further movement. Delivering cargo with a violation is not permitted. (Rules, item 165)

g8-q52.text: If cargo protrudes 0.6 m beyond the rear end of the vehicle, must it be marked during daylight hours with the “Oversized Cargo” identification sign and, at night or under conditions of insufficient visibility, additionally with a white light or reflector at the front and a red light or reflector at the rear?
g8-q52.explanation: No, because cargo must be marked with the "Oversized load" identification sign and lights (reflectors) only if it protrudes beyond the front or rear dimensions by more than 1 m. With a 0.6 m protrusion, additional marking is not required. (Rules, item 162)

g8-q53.text: If cargo protrudes 0.3 m beyond the side of the vehicle, measured from the outer edge of the marker light, must it be marked during daylight hours with the “Oversized Cargo” identification sign and, at night or under conditions of insufficient visibility, additionally with a white light or reflector at the front and a red light or reflector at the rear?
g8-q53.explanation: No, when protruding laterally beyond the outer edge of the position light, cargo is marked with the "Oversized load" identification sign and lights only if it protrudes by more than 0.4 m. With a 0.3 m protrusion, there is no such requirement. (Rules, item 162)

g9-q1.text: When approaching a stopped vehicle with a flashing red beacon switched on, drivers of vehicles proceeding in that direction must:
options: Stop and continue only after receiving permission.
Reduce speed so that they can stop immediately if necessary.
g9-q1.explanation: When approaching a stationary vehicle with a red flashing beacon turned on, drivers traveling in that direction must stop and continue driving only after receiving permission. The requirement to reduce speed applies only when approaching a stationary vehicle with blue or blue-and-red beacons. (Rules, items 30, 31)

g9-q2.text: When a vehicle with a flashing blue beacon and a special audible signal activated is approaching, drivers of vehicles must:
options: Yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle.
Reduce speed and yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle.
g9-q2.explanation: When a vehicle with a blue flashing beacon and a special audible signal approaches, drivers must yield the right of way to ensure its unobstructed passage. Mandatory speed reduction and yielding are required when a vehicle with blue and red flashing beacons and a special audible signal approaches. (Rules, items 28, 29)

g9-q3.text: Is it mandatory to have the low-beam headlights switched on during daylight hours on mopeds?
g9-q3.explanation: Mandatory: to indicate a moving vehicle during daylight hours, low-beam headlights must be turned on on all motorcycles and mopeds. This increases the visibility of two-wheeled vehicles during the day. (Rules, item 133, sub-item 1)

g9-q4.text: In which case do the rules not require a warning signal to be given?
options: Before stopping at the edge of the roadway.
Before a curve in the road within the area of effect of a “Dangerous Turn” sign.
Before changing to an adjacent traffic lane.
g9-q4.explanation: Giving a warning signal is not mandatory if the vehicle travels along a curved section of road without changing lanes (before a curve under the "Dangerous curve" sign). However, when stopping at the edge of the roadway and before changing into an adjacent lane, signaling is mandatory. (Rules, item 36)

g9-q5.text: Before changing lanes, a warning signal must be given:
options: In advance, before beginning the maneuver.
g9-q5.explanation: Before starting to move or performing a maneuver (including changing lanes), a warning signal must be given well in advance before beginning the maneuver. A signal given immediately before or after starting does not ensure timely notification of other drivers. (Rules, item 36)

g9-q6.text: When performing a maneuver, a warning signal must be given:
options: Before changing the direction of traffic.
While changing the direction of traffic.
In advance, before changing the direction of traffic.
g9-q6.explanation: When performing a maneuver, a warning signal must be given well in advance before changing the direction of travel. Signaling while changing direction or at the last moment violates the rules' requirement. (Rules, item 36)

g9-q7.text: A warning signal given by hand must be discontinued:
g9-q7.explanation: A warning signal given by the driver by hand is stopped immediately before beginning the maneuver so that the driver can confidently steer the vehicle with both hands. A signal given by indicator lights is stopped immediately after completing the maneuver. (Rules, item 36)

g9-q8.text: In which case must the driver give a warning signal before stopping?
options: If another vehicle is proceeding behind the driver.
g9-q8.explanation: Before stopping, a driver must give a warning signal in all cases—regardless of whether another vehicle is traveling behind them or not, and whether inside or outside a built-up area. (Rules, item 36)

g9-q9.text: If forced to stop on a railroad crossing, what general alarm signal must the driver give by repeated horn signals?
g9-q9.explanation: In the event of a forced stop on a railway crossing, the driver must stay near the vehicle and give the general alarm signal—a combination of one long and three short audible signals sounded in succession. Other combinations are incorrect. (Rules, item 112)

g9-q10.text: If a turn signal is absent or malfunctioning, a warning signal given by hand must be discontinued:
g9-q10.explanation: If turn indicator lights are absent or malfunctioning, a warning signal given by hand is stopped immediately before beginning the maneuver. Keeping an arm extended during the maneuver is dangerous and prohibited, while stopping the signal after completing the maneuver applies only to indicator lights. (Rules, item 36)

g9-q11.text: The following combination of horn signals constitutes the general alarm signal given at a railroad crossing:
g9-q11.explanation: The general alarm signal given at a railway crossing is a combination of one long and three short audible signals sounded in succession. The other listed combinations are incorrect. (Rules, item 112)

g9-q12.text: In which image is the driver giving a left-turn signal?
g9-q12.explanation: In picture 1, the driver of the red car has extended their left arm out to the side, which corresponds to a left-turn or U-turn signal. In picture 2, the left arm bent upward at the elbow is a right-turn signal, and in picture 3, an arm raised straight up is a braking signal. (Rules, item 37)

g9-q13.text: When approaching a stationary vehicle with a red flashing beacon activated, drivers proceeding in the same direction must:
options: Stop and continue only after receiving permission.
Reduce speed so that they can stop immediately if necessary.
g9-q13.explanation: When approaching a stationary vehicle with a red flashing beacon turned on, drivers traveling in that direction must come to a complete stop and proceed only after receiving permission. Merely reducing speed is sufficient for stationary vehicles with blue or blue-and-red beacons, whereas an active red beacon requires a mandatory stop. (Rules, item 31)

g9-q14.text: For what purpose are orange or yellow flashing beacons installed on vehicles?
options: To obtain right-of-way over other road users.
To warn other road users of danger.
g9-q14.explanation: Orange or yellow flashing beacons are installed on road-construction and cleaning vehicles, as well as vehicles carrying oversized or hazardous cargo, to warn other road users of danger. They do not grant any priority over other road users, so the first option is incorrect. (Rules, item 32)

g9-q15.text: When a vehicle with a blue flashing beacon and a special audible signal activated is approaching, drivers must:
options: Yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle.
Reduce speed and yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle.
g9-q15.explanation: When a vehicle with a blue flashing beacon and a special audible signal approaches, drivers must yield the right of way to ensure its unobstructed passage. The additional requirement to reduce speed mentioned in the second option applies to the approach of escort vehicles with blue and red beacons. (Rules, item 28)

g9-q16.text: The blue automobile will proceed through the intersection:
options: First, simultaneously with the red automobile.
Second, simultaneously with the red automobile.
Third, simultaneously with the red automobile.
g9-q16.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection of equivalent roads, the ambulance with a blue flashing beacon and special audible signal turned on has priority and proceeds first. Then the red and blue cars must yield to the green car approaching from their right (which proceeds second), after which the blue car will cross the intersection third—simultaneously with the red car. (Rules, item 26, item 28, item 98)

g9-q17.text: When a vehicle with blue and red flashing beacons and a special audible signal activated is approaching, drivers must:
options: Yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle.
Reduce speed and yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle and the vehicles it is escorting.
g9-q17.explanation: When a vehicle with blue and red flashing beacons and a special audible signal approaches, drivers must reduce speed and yield the right of way both to that vehicle and to the vehicles it is escorting. The first option is incomplete because it does not account for reducing speed and allowing the escorted convoy unobstructed passage. (Rules, item 29)

g9-q18.text: Which vehicle driver has the right-of-way?
options: The driver of the road-cleaning vehicle.
g9-q18.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection of equivalent roads, the yellow (orange) flashing beacon turned on on the road-cleaning vehicle does not grant priority and serves only as a hazard warning. Since the passenger car is approaching from the right, the passenger car driver has the right of way, and the cleaning vehicle must yield (Rules, items 32, 98).

g9-q19.text: The black automobile will proceed through the intersection:
g9-q19.explanation: The fire truck approaching on the secondary road (sign 2.4) will cross the intersection first, as its blue flashing beacon and special audible signal are turned on. The black and green cars are on the priority road (sign 2.1), but the green car has its left turn indicator on and must yield to the oncoming black car going straight. Consequently, the black car will cross the intersection second (Rules, items 28, 96, 99).

g9-q20.explanation: Although the green traffic light signal is on for the passenger car, the ambulance approaching from the left has its blue flashing beacon and special audible signal turned on. A vehicle with such special signals has the right of priority passage regardless of a red traffic light, so the passenger car driver must yield (Rules, items 26, 28).

g9-q21.text: The blue automobile will proceed through the intersection:
g9-q21.explanation: The yellow special-service car approaching from the right will cross the intersection first thanks to its activated blue flashing beacon and special audible signal. Next, the green (on the right) and red cars will proceed along the main road (signs 2.1 and 8.13), while the blue car turning left from the secondary road has no priority and will cross the intersection last (Rules, items 28, 96, 97, 98).

g9-q22.text: Does an activated yellow (orange) flashing beacon give a vehicle the right-of-way?
