g9-q22.explanation: A yellow or orange flashing beacon does not grant traffic priority. It serves only to attract the attention of other road users and warn of danger, so the driver of such a vehicle cannot demand the right of way. (Rules, item 32)

g9-q23.text: The driver of a vehicle with white flashing beacons activated gives a special audible signal in order to:
options: Obtain right-of-way over other road users.
Attract the attention of police officers and other persons.
g9-q23.explanation: Lunar-white flashing beacons and a special audible signal are switched on only in the event of an attack on that vehicle (for example, a cash-in-transit vehicle) to attract the attention of police officers and other persons. They do not grant traffic priority, which is why the first option is incorrect. (Rules, item 35)

g9-q24.text: The driver of a vehicle equipped with a blue flashing beacon has the right-of-way over other road users if the driver:
options: Is giving a special audible signal.
Has activated the blue flashing beacon and the special audible signal.
g9-q24.explanation: The driver of a vehicle equipped with a blue flashing beacon gains traffic priority only when both the blue beacon and the special audible signal are turned on simultaneously. When activated separately (the first two options), no traffic priority is granted. (Rules, item 26)

g9-q25.text: Within what distance before a railroad crossing is passing prohibited?
g9-q25.explanation: Overtaking is prohibited on railway crossings and within 100 meters before them, as limited visibility and entering the oncoming lane increase the risk of colliding with a train. The 50-meter rule applies to parking prohibitions near crossings, while 150 meters is not a limit established by the rules. (Rules, item 77)

g9-q26.text: Is passing vehicles at an intersection permitted when proceeding on a road that is the priority road relative to the intersecting road?
g9-q26.explanation: Under the Road Traffic Rules of the Republic of Armenia, overtaking is prohibited at all intersections regardless of whether the vehicle is on a main or secondary road. Because of intersecting oncoming or cross traffic at an intersection, overtaking creates an emergency situation, so the permitting option is incorrect. (Rules, item 77)

g9-q27.text: Is the passenger-car driver permitted to pass in the indicated situation?
options: Permitted if the motorcycle’s speed does not exceed 30 km/h.
g9-q27.explanation: In the depicted situation, the driver of the motorcycle with a sidecar is already overtaking the truck with a trailer. Overtaking is prohibited if the driver of the vehicle being overtaken is themselves overtaking or bypassing an obstacle, and the motorcycle's speed (up to 30 km/h) provides no exception (Rules, item 77, sub-item 4).

g9-q28.explanation: Overtaking is prohibited at intersections in all cases. Before railway crossings, overtaking is prohibited only within 100 m, not 150 m, so the second and third options are incorrect. (Rules, item 77)

g9-q29.explanation: Under the rules, overtaking is prohibited at both controlled and uncontrolled intersections without exception. Therefore, options mentioning only one type of intersection are incomplete, and "In both cases" is the correct answer. (Rules, item 77)

g9-q30.text: Is it permitted to pass the road train in this situation if its speed does not exceed 30 km/h?
g9-q30.explanation: Sign 1.6 "Intersection of equal roads" placed on the right warns of an intersection ahead that is already visible on the road. Overtaking at intersections is prohibited regardless of the speed of the road train being overtaken, so a speed of up to 30 km/h does not permit overtaking (Rules, item 77, sub-item 1).

g9-q31.text: Is the driver of the green automobile permitted to pass?
options: Permitted if the red automobile is proceeding at a speed below 30 km/h.
g9-q31.explanation: With sign 1.25 "Road works" and a barrier, the right lane is closed, creating a road narrowing, and vehicles ahead are bypassing the obstacle. Overtaking is prohibited at road narrowings and when the vehicle ahead is bypassing an obstacle or overtaking, regardless of the red car's speed (Rules, item 77, sub-items 4 and 5).

g9-q32.text: Is the driver of the red automobile permitted to pass in this situation?
options: Permitted if the speed of the automobile being passed does not exceed 30 km/h.
g9-q32.explanation: Although the red car and the truck are on the main road (sign 2.1), they are immediately entering an intersection. Under RA rules, overtaking at intersections is prohibited in all cases—even on a main road and regardless of the speed of the vehicle ahead (Rules, item 77, sub-item 1).

g9-q33.text: Is it permitted to pass the bus at the indicated location?
g9-q33.explanation: In this section, warning signs 1.2 "Railway crossing without barrier" and 1.4.1 (1.4.4) with three diagonal stripes "Approach to railway crossing" are installed, which outside built-up areas are placed 150–300 m before the crossing. Since overtaking is prohibited on railway crossings and closer than 100 m before them, overtaking the bus at the indicated location is permitted (Rules, item 77, sub-item 3).

options: Proceeding ahead of one or more moving vehicles by leaving the occupied lane and entering the oncoming traffic lane.
Proceeding ahead of one or more moving vehicles by leaving the occupied lane.
g9-q34.explanation: According to the current definition, overtaking is passing one or more moving vehicles associated with leaving the occupied traffic lane. The definition does not require necessarily entering the oncoming lane, so the first option mistakenly narrows the concept. (Rules, item 3)

g9-q35.text: At night and under conditions of insufficient visibility, regardless of road lighting, moving motor vehicles must have the following activated:
g9-q35.explanation: During dark hours and in conditions of insufficient visibility, regardless of road lighting, motor vehicles must have their high-beam or low-beam headlights turned on. Options mentioning only one type of light are incorrect, as the choice of light depends on road lighting and the possibility of dazzling other drivers. (Rules, item 127)

g9-q36.text: In which case must a motorcycle have its low-beam headlights activated during daylight?
options: When proceeding under conditions of insufficient visibility.
When proceeding to a parking location on a motorcycle with a malfunction.
In all cases while participating in traffic.
g9-q36.explanation: During daylight hours, low-beam headlights on motorcycles (and mopeds) must be turned on in all cases while in traffic. This ensures good visibility of a small-sized vehicle, so the other options mentioning only specific cases are incorrect. (Rules, item 133)

g9-q37.text: What must the driver do first if dazzled by the headlights of an oncoming vehicle?
options: Switch the high-beam headlights (if activated) to low beam.
Give a horn signal consisting of one long and three short signals.
Give a horn signal consisting of one short and three long signals.
g9-q37.explanation: If dazzled by the headlights of an oncoming vehicle, the driver must first turn on the hazard warning lights and, without changing lanes, reduce speed or stop. Switching headlights does not warn following drivers, while one long and three short audible signals are used during a forced stop at a railway crossing. (Rules, item 129)

g9-q38.text: Horn signals may be used only:
options: In populated areas, to warn other drivers of the intention to pass.
When necessary to prevent a traffic accident.
g9-q38.explanation: In built-up areas, sounding the horn is permitted only when necessary to prevent a road traffic accident. Warning of an intent to overtake with an audible signal is permitted only outside built-up areas, so the first and third options are incorrect. (Rules, item 136)

g9-q39.text: At night, on unlit sections of road, a moving motor vehicle must have the following activated:
g9-q39.explanation: When driving on unlit sections of road during dark hours, a motor vehicle must have its high-beam or low-beam headlights turned on. Driving only with high beams or only with low beams is unacceptable, as lights must be switched depending on the presence of oncoming or same-direction vehicles. (Rules, item 127)

g9-q40.text: Rear fog lights may be used:
options: At night when proceeding as part of a convoy.
Only under conditions of insufficient visibility.
At night when unloading a vehicle.
In all of the listed cases.
g9-q40.explanation: Rear fog lights may be used only in conditions of insufficient visibility (fog, heavy rain, snowfall). Turning them on simply at night, in a tunnel, or while unloading is prohibited, as the bright red light dazzles following drivers. (Rules, item 131)

g9-q41.text: At what distance from an oncoming vehicle must high-beam headlights be switched to low beam?
g9-q41.explanation: To avoid dazzling an oncoming vehicle, high-beam headlights must be switched to low-beam at a distance of at least 150 m from it. 100 meters is too short a distance and already dazzles the driver, while 300 meters is not a mandatory minimum threshold. (Rules, item 128)

options: Only outside populated areas when there are no oncoming or preceding vehicles.
Only under conditions of insufficient visibility.
At night on all sections of road.
g9-q42.explanation: A searchlight (spotlight) may be used only outside built-up areas in the absence of oncoming and same-direction vehicles, as its bright directed beam dazzles other drivers. Inside built-up areas, only vehicles with special beacons may use it while performing official duties. (Rules, item 134)

g9-q43.text: In populated areas, at what distance before the beginning of a hazardous section is this warning sign installed?
g9-q43.explanation: The image shows warning sign 1.23 "Children". In built-up areas, warning signs (except repeated signs or cases where another distance is indicated by plate 8.1.1) are installed 50–100 m before the start of the hazardous section, whereas the 100–150 m option is incorrect (Rules, item 166, sign 1.23).

g9-q44.text: Is it permitted to transport agricultural, road-construction, construction, and other machines and mechanisms across a railroad crossing?
options: Permitted if the crossing is not equipped with a barrier gate.
Permitted if they are in a non-transport position.
Permitted if they are in a transport position.
g9-q44.explanation: Transporting agricultural, road, construction, and other machines and mechanisms across a railway crossing is permitted only when they are in transport condition. In non-transport condition, they can damage the track, road surface, or overhead contact line regardless of whether a barrier is present. (Rules, item 114)

g9-q45.text: Where is it permitted to cross railroad tracks?
options: At locations where visibility in both directions is at least 1,000 m.
At locations most convenient at the driver’s discretion.
At least 1,000 m from railroad stations.
g9-q45.explanation: Drivers are permitted to cross railway tracks only at designated and equipped locations—railway crossings. Crossing tracks elsewhere, regardless of visibility or distance from a station, is strictly prohibited due to the high risk of an accident. (Rules, item 109)

g9-q46.text: While performing an official assignment, is it permitted to open or bypass a barrier gate without authorization?
options: Permitted at the driver’s discretion if no train is approaching nearby.
Permitted if the railroad crossing attendant is absent.
g9-q46.explanation: Even while performing an official duty, it is prohibited to arbitrarily open or bypass a closed barrier. Rail transport has unconditional priority, and such actions—even in the absence of a crossing attendant or with a seemingly clear track—create a life-threatening hazard. (Rules, items 113, 114)

g9-q47.text: Is it permitted to transport agricultural, road-construction, construction, and other machines and mechanisms across a railroad crossing?
options: Permitted if they are in a transport position.
g9-q47.explanation: Agricultural, road, construction, and other machines and mechanisms may be transported across a railway crossing only when in transport condition. Without this condition or in non-transport condition, transport is prohibited because the mechanisms can damage the crossing or block the rails. (Rules, item 114)

g9-q48.text: What must the driver follow when approaching a railroad crossing?
options: The position of the barrier gate and the traffic signals.
The requirements of traffic signs and pavement markings.
The instructions of the railroad crossing attendant.
g9-q48.explanation: When approaching a railway crossing, the driver must simultaneously be guided by the position of the barrier, traffic light signals, requirements of road signs and markings, and instructions of the crossing attendant. Following only one requirement is insufficient, as all listed rules are mandatory for safely yielding to a train. (Rules, item 110)

g9-q49.text: Are pedestrians permitted to proceed on a road marked with the “Freeway” sign?
options: Permitted outside populated areas, against the direction of vehicle traffic.
Permitted outside populated areas, in the same direction as vehicle traffic.
g9-q49.explanation: Pedestrian movement along roads equipped with the "Motorway" sign is prohibited without exception. The high permitted speeds on motorways make the presence of pedestrians dangerous both moving with and against the flow of traffic. (Rules, item 116)

g9-q50.text: Vehicles whose speed, because of their technical characteristics or condition, does not exceed 40 km/h are:
options: Permitted on freeways only in the rightmost lane.
Permitted on freeways if there is no “Minimum Speed Limit” sign.
g9-q50.explanation: Vehicles whose speed, due to technical specifications or condition, does not exceed 40 km/h are prohibited from driving on motorways. Driving in the rightmost lane or when no sign is present is also prohibited, as slow-moving vehicles create obstacles and accident hazards in high-speed traffic. (Rules, item 116)

g9-q51.text: The hazard warning lights on a vehicle must be activated:
options: In the event of a traffic accident.
In the event of a forced stop where stopping is prohibited.
g9-q51.explanation: Hazard warning lights must be turned on both in the event of a road traffic accident and during a forced stop in places where stopping is prohibited. This gives timely warning to other drivers about an unexpected obstacle, so "In both cases" is correct. (Rules, item 22)

g9-q52.text: The hazard warning lights on a vehicle must be activated:
options: In the event of a traffic accident.
During towing, on the towed motor vehicle.
In the event of a forced stop where stopping is prohibited.
In all of the listed cases.
g9-q52.explanation: Hazard warning lights on a vehicle must be turned on during an RTA, during towing (on the towed motor vehicle), and during a forced stop in places where stopping is prohibited. Signaling danger is mandatory in all listed situations, so individual options are incomplete. (Rules, item 22)

g9-q53.text: At what distance from the vehicle must the emergency warning triangle be placed?
options: At least 15 m in populated areas and at least 30 m outside populated areas.
At least 10 m in populated areas and at least 20 m outside populated areas.
At least 5 m in populated areas and at least 10 m outside populated areas.
g9-q53.explanation: The "Emergency stop" warning triangle is placed at a distance of not less than 15 m from the vehicle in built-up areas, and not less than 30 m outside built-up areas. Smaller distances (5–10 m or 10–20 m) do not give approaching drivers enough time to notice the obstacle and stop. (Rules, item 23)

g9-q54.text: The hazard warning lights on a vehicle must be activated:
options: If the driver is dazzled by headlights.
During towing, on the towed motor vehicle.
g9-q54.explanation: Hazard warning lights must be turned on both when the driver is dazzled by headlights and during towing—on the towed motor vehicle. In both situations it is necessary to warn other road users, so the third option is correct. (Rules, item 22)

g9-q55.text: The hazard warning lights on a vehicle must be activated:
options: In the event of a traffic accident.
During towing, on the towed motor vehicle.
g9-q55.explanation: Hazard warning lights must be turned on both in the event of a road traffic accident and during towing (on the towed motor vehicle). This ensures the visibility of a hazardous situation to other drivers, so selecting only one case is incomplete. (Rules, item 22)

g9-q56.text: In developed areas where the entrance and exit are marked by the “Residential Zone” and “End of Residential Zone” traffic signs, the following is not prohibited:
g9-q56.explanation: In areas designated by the "Residential zone" sign, pedestrians are not prohibited from walking on the roadway and have priority. Through traffic and driving instruction in residential zones are explicitly prohibited. (Rules, items 119, 121)

g9-q57.text: An intersection is considered controlled if the order of traffic is determined by:
g9-q57.explanation: An intersection is considered controlled if the order of traffic is determined either by traffic light signals or by a traffic controller's signals. Therefore, the options "Only traffic light" or "Only traffic controller" are incomplete, and "In both cases" is correct. (Rules, item 89)

g9-q58.text: On an unpaved dirt road, does the presence of a paved section immediately before an intersection make that road equal in priority to the intersecting road?
g9-q58.explanation: The presence of a paved section immediately before an intersection on an unpaved dirt road does not make that road equal in status to the intersecting hard-surfaced road. Such asphalted sections are intended to prevent carrying dirt and mud onto the main road, so the road remains secondary. (Rules, item 3)

g9-q59.text: Which image shows the permitted directions of traffic?
g9-q59.explanation: In all three pictures, sign 3.19 "U-turn prohibited" is placed before the intersection, which prohibits only U-turns and does not prohibit left turns. The left and middle pictures mistakenly show a U-turn arrow, so the permitted directions (straight, left, and right) are shown correctly only in the right picture (Rules, item 166, sign 3.19).

g9-q60.text: If the meanings of the traffic signals conflict with the requirements of the priority signs, drivers must follow:
g9-q60.explanation: If traffic light signals contradict the requirements of priority signs, drivers must obey the traffic light signals. Priority signs apply only at uncontrolled intersections when the traffic light is not working or a flashing yellow signal is on. (Rules, item 173)

g9-q61.text: Is the driver permitted to continue when the yellow traffic signal turns on or the traffic controller raises an arm?
options: Permitted if the driver cannot stop without sudden braking.
g9-q61.explanation: When the yellow traffic light comes on or the traffic controller raises their hand, continuing is permitted only to drivers who cannot stop at the designated place without sudden braking. Prohibiting it in all cases creates a risk of rear-end collision, so the first option is incorrect. (Rules, item 19)

g9-q62.text: A traffic controller gives a whistle signal:
options: Only when requiring a vehicle to stop.
To attract the attention of road users.
g9-q62.explanation: The traffic controller gives a whistle signal to draw road users' attention. The whistle itself is not a mandatory stop command; the command to stop a vehicle is given by the traffic controller with a hand or baton. (Rules, item 17)

g9-q63.text: In this situation, is the road train permitted to proceed across the bridge?
g9-q63.explanation: Sign 3.11 "Mass limit" placed before the bridge prohibits the movement of vehicles, including road trains, whose total actual mass exceeds 5 tonnes. Since the total actual mass of the depicted road train is 9 tonnes (truck 5 t and trailer 4 t), crossing the bridge is prohibited (Rules, item 166, sign 3.11).

g9-q64.text: May a warning signal be given by hand in order to proceed along the indicated path?
options: Yes, if the turn signal is malfunctioning.
Yes, if the turn signal is malfunctioning during daylight hours.
g9-q64.explanation: The driver of the red car warns of the intention to move left with an extended left arm. Before starting to move or performing a maneuver, the driver must signal with a turn indicator, while hand signaling is permitted only when the light indicator is absent or faulty—regardless of the time of day (Rules, item 36).

g9-q65.text: Must the driver activate the turn signal before starting to move in a residential zone?
options: Yes, if other vehicles are present.
g9-q65.explanation: The driver must turn on the turn indicator before starting to move, regardless of whether they are in a residential zone and whether there are other vehicles nearby. The other options ignore the mandatory rule to inform nearby pedestrians and drivers in advance. (Rules, item 36)

g9-q66.text: To obtain right-of-way over other road users, the driver of a patrol vehicle must activate:
options: The blue and red flashing beacons.
The blue flashing beacon and the special audible signal.
g9-q66.explanation: To gain priority over other road users, the driver of a patrol service vehicle must turn on the blue flashing beacon and the special audible signal. Flashing beacons alone, without a special audible signal, do not provide traffic priority. (Rules, item 26)

options: At railroad crossings and within 100 m before them.
At railroad crossings and within 150 m before them.
At railroad crossings and within 250 m before them.
g9-q67.explanation: Overtaking is prohibited on railway crossings and within 100 m before them. The 150 m and 250 m options are false limits and do not match the distance established in the rules. (Rules, item 77)

g9-q68.text: What does the hand signal given by the passenger-car driver indicate?
options: The driver is making a right turn.
The driver is continuing straight ahead.
g9-q68.explanation: The driver of the white car ahead has extended their left arm vertically upward. A right or left arm raised upward is the braking signal, with which the driver informs of reducing speed or stopping (for a right turn, the left arm is bent at the elbow at a right angle) (Rules, item 37).

g9-q69.text: The hazard warning lights must be activated:
options: In the event of a traffic accident.
When proceeding as part of an organized convoy.
g9-q69.explanation: Hazard warning lights must be turned on in the event of a road traffic accident. Before entering a tunnel and when driving in an organized column, low-beam or high-beam headlights must be turned on, not hazard warning lights. (Rules, item 22)

g9-q70.text: What does the hand signal given by the motorcycle operator indicate?
options: The motorcycle will proceed to the left or make a U-turn.
The motorcycle will proceed straight ahead or to the right.
g9-q70.explanation: The motorcycle rider has extended their left arm horizontally to the side. A left arm extended to the side corresponds to a left turn or U-turn signal, meaning the driver intends to travel to the left or in the opposite direction (Rules, item 37).

g9-q71.text: What does the hand signal given by the passenger-car driver indicate?
options: The driver is making a right turn.
The driver is continuing straight ahead.
The driver is braking in order to yield to the motorcycle.
g9-q71.explanation: The driver of the passenger car ahead has bent their left arm upward at the elbow at a right angle. This position corresponds to a right turn signal, whereas to give a braking signal the arm is extended straight upward (Rules, item 37).

g9-q72.text: What does the hand signal given by the passenger-car driver indicate?
options: The driver intends to make a left turn or a U-turn.
The driver is braking in order to yield to the truck.
g9-q72.explanation: The driver of the white car has extended their left arm to the left side. A left arm directed to the side informs of an intention to make a left turn or U-turn, whereas for braking the arm is raised straight upward (Rules, item 37).

g9-q73.text: In this case, must the driver activate the turn signal?
g9-q73.explanation: Mandatory sign 4.1.2 "Proceed right" is installed before the intersection, requiring a right turn. Regardless of the presence of a mandatory sign, before performing a maneuver (a right turn) the driver must turn on the turn indicator for the corresponding direction in advance (Rules, item 36).

g9-q74.text: Is the truck driver permitted to pass the bus that is proceeding at a speed of 60 km/h?
g9-q74.explanation: The "GYUMRI" sign on a blue background installed on the right side of the road shows that built-up area speed limits do not apply on this section, and the truck's permitted speed exceeds the bus's 60 km/h speed. Since the lane marking is broken, the oncoming lane is clear, and there are no signs prohibiting overtaking, the truck driver is permitted to overtake the bus (Rules, items 69, 73).

g9-q75.text: Is passing permitted in this situation?
options: Permitted if the bus is proceeding at a speed below 30 km/h.
g9-q75.explanation: In a built-up area, sign 1.2 "Railway crossing without barrier" is installed 50–100 m before the crossing, which means the car is already less than 100 m from the railway crossing. On railway crossings and within 100 m before them, overtaking is prohibited regardless of the bus's speed (Rules, item 77, sub-item 3).

g9-q76.text: Is it permitted to enter the railroad crossing in this situation?
g9-q76.explanation: Although the railway crossing barriers are open, the crossing attendant is standing facing the driver and extending a red flag to the side. On a prohibiting signal from the crossing attendant, entering the railway crossing is strictly prohibited (Rules, item 113, sub-item 5).

g9-q77.text: Is it permitted to enter the railroad crossing in this situation?
options: Permitted if no train is approaching.
Permitted if the barrier gate is open.
g9-q77.explanation: The traffic light installed before the railway crossing shows a prohibiting red signal. On a prohibiting traffic light signal, entering the crossing is prohibited regardless of the open position of the barrier and the absence of a train within visibility range (Rules, item 113, sub-item 2).

g9-q78.text: What should the driver do in this situation?
options: If no train is approaching, go around the barrier gate and continue.
Stop and wait for the barrier gate to open.
g9-q78.explanation: In the depicted situation, the railway crossing barrier is closed. When the barrier is closed or closing, entering the crossing is prohibited regardless of the traffic light signal, and bypassing or arbitrarily opening the barrier is also prohibited, so the driver must stop and wait for the barrier to open (Rules, items 111, 113, 114).

g9-q79.text: In this situation, is it permitted to cross the railroad crossing?
options: Permitted if no train is approaching.
g9-q79.explanation: The truck immediately beyond the railway crossing has its brake lights on (stopped before sign 2.4 "Give way"), and there is insufficient space behind it to clear the crossing. If congestion or a stop beyond the crossing would force the driver to stop on the railway crossing, entering the crossing is prohibited (Rules, item 113, sub-item 3).

g9-q80.text: In this situation, is it permitted to cross the railroad crossing?
options: Permitted if no train is approaching.
Permitted because the railroad crossing attendant is prohibiting the oncoming vehicle from crossing.
g9-q80.explanation: Although the barriers are open and the traffic light does not prohibit movement, the crossing attendant is giving a prohibiting signal with a red flag. On the attendant's prohibiting signal, crossing the railway crossing is prohibited regardless of the absence of an approaching train or the position of the oncoming vehicle (Rules, items 110, 113, sub-item 5).

g9-q81.text: In this situation, where may passing be started?
options: After proceeding 100 m beyond the railroad crossing.
g9-q81.explanation: Overtaking is prohibited on railway crossings and within 100 m before them. However, immediately after passing the crossing this prohibition ceases to apply, so overtaking may begin right after passing the railway crossing (there is no requirement to wait 100 m) (Rules, item 77, sub-item 3).

g9-q82.text: In this situation, is passing permitted?
options: Permitted because there is no oncoming vehicle.
Permitted if the animal-drawn cart is moving at a speed below 30 km/h.
g9-q82.explanation: Due to the green car making an emergency stop in the right lane, a narrowing of the roadway has occurred, and the dump truck and animal-drawn cart ahead are bypassing the obstacle. In such a situation, overtaking is prohibited at road narrowings and when the vehicle being overtaken is bypassing an obstacle—regardless of the absence of oncoming vehicles or the cart's speed (Rules, item 77, sub-items 4 and 5).

g9-q83.text: What maneuver is the passenger-car driver performing?
g9-q83.explanation: The passenger car driver has turned on the left turn indicator and, leaving the occupied lane, is passing the moving truck. Passing without leaving the occupied lane is passing within lanes, passing a stationary object is bypassing, whereas passing a moving vehicle by leaving the occupied lane is called overtaking (Rules, item 3, sub-item 11).

g9-q84.explanation: An uncontrolled intersection with intersecting roads is visible ahead, where a yellow minibus is also traveling from the right. Under RA rules, overtaking at intersections is prohibited in all cases, so overtaking the motorcycle is not permitted (Rules, item 77, sub-item 1).

g9-q85.text: On a road with one lane in each direction, when is passing in the oncoming traffic lane permitted?
options: Only when the oncoming traffic lane is clear for a sufficient distance.
Only when no vehicle is passing us.
g9-q85.explanation: On a road with one lane in each direction, overtaking via the oncoming lane may be performed only if both the oncoming lane is clear for a sufficient distance and no one is overtaking us (and the vehicle ahead has not signaled overtaking or a left turn). Ensuring only one of these conditions can lead to a head-on or side collision. (Rules, item 73)

g9-q86.text: Is passing permitted in the indicated situation?
options: Permitted if the maneuver can be completed within the visible section of the road.
g9-q86.explanation: On the road section with sign 1.14 "Steep ascent" on the right, the road marking is broken, the road is straight, and visibility is ensured for a long distance. Overtaking is prohibited only at the end of an ascent and on sections with limited visibility, so at the start of the ascent with sufficient visibility, overtaking is permitted (Rules, item 77, sub-item 8).

options: Yes, if the passing maneuver is completed before the intersection.
g9-q87.explanation: Outside built-up areas, warning sign 1.6 "Intersection of equal roads" is installed 150–300 m before the intersection. Since the intersection is still ahead and overtaking at intersections is prohibited, overtaking the truck is permitted only on condition that overtaking is completed before the intersection (Rules, item 77, sub-item 1).

g9-q88.text: What is required of the driver of the vehicle being passed?
options: The driver must yield to the passing vehicle.
The driver must not interfere with the passing vehicle by increasing speed or by taking any other action.
g9-q88.explanation: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken must not impede the overtaking driver in any way by increasing speed or performing other actions. In general, they are not obliged to stop or yield the road (this is required only of slow-moving or oversized vehicles outside built-up areas), so the first option is incorrect. (Rules, item 75)

g9-q89.text: Is passing permitted in this situation?
options: Permitted if the truck is moving at less than 30 km/h.
g9-q89.explanation: Sign 3.20 "Overtaking prohibited" on the right prohibits overtaking all types of vehicles except slow-moving vehicles, animal-drawn vehicles, mopeds, bicycles, and two-wheeled motorcycles without a sidecar. An ordinary truck is not classified as a slow-moving vehicle merely for traveling at less than 30 km/h, so overtaking is prohibited (Rules, item 166, sign 3.20).

g9-q90.text: Is the driver of a truck with a maximum authorized mass of 3 metric tons permitted to pass the tractor?
options: Yes, if the tractor is moving at less than 30 km/h.
g9-q90.explanation: Sign 3.22 "Overtaking by trucks prohibited" on the right applies only to trucks with a maximum permissible mass exceeding 3.5 tonnes. Since this truck's maximum permissible mass is 3 tonnes, the sign's prohibition does not apply to it, and overtaking the tractor is permitted (Rules, item 166, sign 3.22).

g9-q91.text: If oncoming traffic is difficult in this situation, who must yield?
g9-q91.explanation: Sign 1.14 "Steep ascent" (12%) on the right side of the road shows that the passenger car is traveling uphill, while the oncoming truck is traveling downhill. On longitudinal slopes equipped with signs 1.13 and 1.14, when oncoming passage is difficult, the driver traveling downhill—that is, the truck driver—must yield the road (Rules, item 46).

g9-q92.text: Passing at a pedestrian crossing is:
options: Prohibited only when pedestrians are present.
g9-q92.explanation: Overtaking on a pedestrian crossing is prohibited in all cases, regardless of whether there is a pedestrian on the crossing or not. The vehicle being overtaken can block the field of view and hide a pedestrian entering the crossing, so the first and third options are dangerous and incorrect. (Rules, item 77)

g9-q93.text: Along which path is passing permitted?
g9-q93.explanation: Along the depicted trajectory A, the driver overtakes the first truck and returns to their lane before the intersection, whereas along trajectory B overtaking continues directly across the intersection. Since overtaking at intersections is prohibited, overtaking is permitted only along trajectory A (Rules, item 77, sub-item 1).

g9-q94.text: What does the traffic sign indicate?
options: There is a fallen tree 500 meters ahead.
There is a rest area 500 meters ahead.
There is a rest area along the next 500 meters.
g9-q94.explanation: Service sign 7.11 "Rest area" is installed on the right side of the road, and the "500m" inscription at the bottom indicates the distance remaining to the rest area. Consequently, the sign informs that a rest area is located 500 meters ahead (not the length of a section or a fallen tree) (Rules, item 166, sign 7.11).

g9-q95.text: In this situation, is the driver required to activate the turn signal?
options: Yes, if a vehicle is approaching from behind.
g9-q95.explanation: On this curved section of road equipped with sign 1.11.1 "Dangerous bend", there is no intersection and the driver is not changing lanes. If a vehicle travels along a curved section in the road plan without changing lanes, turning on the turn indicator is not mandatory (Rules, item 36).

g9-q96.text: By raising an arm, the driver indicates:
options: An intention to make a left turn.
An intention to proceed straight ahead.
g9-q96.explanation: The driver of the blue car approaching the intersection (sign 2.4 "Give way") has extended their left arm straight upward. A right or left arm extended upward informs of slowing down—braking (to yield to the motorcycle approaching from the left)—rather than turning left or going straight (Rules, item 37).

options: Gives the driver the right-of-way over other road users.
Does not give the driver the right-of-way over other road users.
Gives the driver the right-of-way only when starting to move.
g9-q97.explanation: A turn signal or hand signal only warns other road users of the driver's intention and grants no priority. A signaling driver, including when starting to move, must yield in the manner prescribed by the rules, so the other two options are incorrect. (Rules, item 36)

g9-q98.text: When making a right turn while following the priority road, giving a turn signal is:
g9-q98.explanation: Signs 2.1 "Main road" and 8.13 "Direction of main road" installed before the intersection show that the main road turns right. Regardless of traveling on the main road and the time of day, making a right turn at an intersection is a maneuver, so giving the appropriate signal is mandatory (Rules, item 36).

g9-q99.text: What is the driver of the motorcycle indicating?
options: An intention to continue straight ahead.
An intention to make a left turn.
An intention to slow down in order to yield to the passenger car.
g9-q99.explanation: The motorcycle rider ahead has raised their left arm upward while approaching an intersection of equal roads where a passenger car is approaching from the right. A raised arm is the braking signal, meaning the motorcycle rider is signaling a reduction in speed in order to yield to the passenger car approaching from the right (Rules, items 37, 98).

g9-q100.text: In this situation, when making a left turn, giving a turn signal is:
g9-q100.explanation: Signs 2.1 and 8.13 show that the main road turns left at the intersection. Since a left turn is a change of direction (maneuver), signaling a left turn is mandatory even when continuing along the direction of the main road (Rules, item 36).

g9-q101.text: When passing, the left turn signal must be turned off:
options: Immediately after changing to the left lane.
Only after proceeding ahead of the vehicle in front.
g9-q101.explanation: The blue car has turned on its left turn indicator and is changing into the left lane to overtake the truck. The signal must be stopped immediately after completing the maneuver, so the left turn indicator must be turned off right after changing into the left lane so as not to confuse other drivers (Rules, item 36).

g9-q102.text: When making a U-turn at this intersection, which turn signal must be activated?
g9-q102.explanation: Sign 4.3 "Roundabout" is installed before the intersection. When entering a roundabout intersection, the vehicle initially turns to the right, so to make a U-turn, the right turn indicator must be turned on when entering the intersection (Rules, item 36).

g9-q103.text: In the indicated situation, must you give a turn signal?
options: Yes, if there is a driver proceeding in the right lane.
g9-q103.explanation: Overhead sign 5.15.5 "End of lane" and road marking 1.19 require changing from the left lane into the right lane. Before executing a maneuver—a lane change—the driver must give a right turn light signal regardless of whether another driver is traveling in the right lane or not (Rules, item 36).

g9-q104.text: What is the driver of the motorcycle indicating?
options: An intention to continue straight ahead.
An intention to make a right turn.
An intention to make a left turn or U-turn.
g9-q104.explanation: The motorcycle rider has extended their left arm straight out to the side. A left arm extended to the side corresponds to a left turn or U-turn signal, whereas no signal is given when driving straight, and for a right turn the left arm is bent or the right arm is extended (Rules, item 37).

g9-q105.text: The turn signal must be canceled
g9-q105.explanation: A maneuver signal given with a light indicator must be stopped immediately after completing the maneuver. Turning it off before or during the maneuver violates the warning, while leaving it on after completion confuses other drivers. (Rules, item 36)

g9-q106.text: In the indicated situation, giving a turn signal is:
g9-q106.explanation: The road marking arrow shows that the driver is changing into the left lane to bypass the animals on the roadway. A lane change is a maneuver, so signaling with the appropriate turn indicator beforehand is mandatory and is not left to the driver's discretion (Rules, item 36).

g9-q107.text: Which driver is giving a right-turn signal?
options: Only the driver on the right.
Only the driver on the left.
g9-q107.explanation: The rider of the left motorcycle has bent their left arm upward at a right angle at the elbow, while the rider of the right motorcycle has extended their right arm to the side. Both a right arm directed to the side and a left arm bent upward at a right angle at the elbow indicate a right turn signal, so both drivers are signaling a right turn (Rules, item 37).

g9-q108.text: When maneuvering in parking areas or at gas stations, you:
options: Are not required to use the turn signal.
g9-q108.explanation: Even when maneuvering in parking lots or gas stations, the driver must signal with the turn indicator. This rule applies everywhere—on any traffic section and on adjacent territories—because other drivers and pedestrians must be informed of the maneuver's direction. (Rules, item 36)

g9-q109.text: In this situation, what can the driver’s outstretched arm indicate?
g9-q109.explanation: The driver of the silver car stopped on the shoulder has extended their left arm out of the window to the side. When pulling onto the roadway from a stopping or parking spot (changing lanes to the left), this signifies their signal of starting to move, whereas the stopping (braking) signal is an arm extended upward (Rules, items 36, 37).

g9-q110.text: Which turn signals must you use when making a U-turn along the indicated path?
g9-q110.explanation: Along the U-turn trajectory shown by the arrow, the driver first moves closer to the right edge of the roadway (a right lane change), then turns left to complete the U-turn. Since a signal for the corresponding direction must be given before each stage of the maneuver, the driver must turn on first the right and then the left turn indicator (Rules, item 36).

g9-q111.text: If you intend to stop immediately after the intersection, when should you activate the right turn signal so as not to mislead other road users?
g9-q111.explanation: If the right turn indicator is turned on in advance—before the intersection—the driver of the black car approaching on the intersecting road may think you intend to turn right at the intersection (even though sign 3.18.1 prohibits a right turn). To avoid confusing road users, the indicator must be turned on after entering the intersection (Rules, item 36).

g9-q112.text: When changing back into the lane proceeding in the same direction after completing a passing maneuver, does the driver have the right-of-way over a driver already proceeding in that lane?
g9-q112.explanation: The driver of the pink car finishing an overtake has turned on the right turn indicator to move back into their lane. When changing lanes, the driver must yield to the blue car traveling in the adjacent lane without changing direction and has no priority (Rules, items 39, 73).

g9-q113.text: Must we yield to a driver exiting an adjacent area with flashing beacons and a special audible signal activated?
g9-q113.explanation: Although ordinary vehicles exiting an adjacent territory must yield to those traveling along the road, the police car exiting from the left has its special light and audible signals turned on. When a vehicle with such signals on approaches, drivers must yield regardless of its direction of travel (Rules, items 28, 29).

g9-q114.text: When proceeding straight through the intersection, must we yield to the driver of the truck with flashing yellow beacons activated?
g9-q114.explanation: When going straight at this intersection, we are on the main road (sign 2.1), while the oncoming truck has its yellow flashing beacons turned on. Yellow or orange flashing beacons do not grant traffic priority, so when going straight we are not required to yield to the truck driver (Rules, items 32, 99).

g9-q115.text: In this situation, to whom must you yield?
options: The driver of the automobile with special light and audible signals activated.
g9-q115.explanation: The intersection is controlled by a traffic light whose green signal supersedes sign 2.1 "Main road". When turning left on a green signal, we must yield to the oncoming motorcycle going straight, and we must also yield to the police car approaching from the left on a red light with special light and audible signals turned on—that is, to both drivers (Rules, items 28, 29, 90, 173).

options: The driver of the truck with a flashing yellow beacon.
g9-q116.explanation: On the green signal of a working traffic light, the requirement of sign 2.4 "Give way" does not apply. When turning left, we must yield to the oncoming bus going straight, whereas the truck approaching from the right is stopped before a red signal and its yellow flashing beacon grants no priority, so we yield only to the bus driver (Rules, items 32, 90, 173).

options: You will proceed through the intersection first.
You must yield to the driver approaching from the left.
g9-q117.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection of equal roads, the driver approaching from the left would normally have to yield to us, but the police car approaching from the left has its blue flashing beacon and special audible signal turned on. Therefore, we cannot cross the intersection first and must yield to the driver approaching from the left (Rules, item 28).

options: The driver of the police automobile.
g9-q118.explanation: The traffic lights are turned off, so signs 2.1 and 8.13 apply, under which the main road turns left from our side. The oncoming truck on the secondary road must yield to us, whereas the police car approaching from the right has its blue flashing beacon and special audible signal turned on, so we must yield only to the police car driver (Rules, items 28, 95, 96).

options: You will proceed through the intersection first.
You will yield only to the driver of the police automobile.
You will yield to all drivers.
g9-q119.explanation: The traffic light is working at the intersection, so under its green signal the requirements of signs 2.1 and 8.13 do not apply. When turning left, we must yield to the oncoming black car going straight, and we must yield to the police car approaching from the right because of its activated special light and audible signals—meaning we will yield to all drivers (Rules, items 28, 90, 173).

g10-q1.text: When providing first aid to a person with a head injury, you should:
options: Lay the person down with the legs raised.
Lay the person down with the head and torso raised, in a semi-reclined position.
Lay the person flat in a horizontal position.
g10-q1.explanation: In the event of a head injury, the casualty should be laid down with the head and torso slightly elevated (in a semi-reclined position). This reduces blood flow to the head and prevents an increase in intracranial pressure, whereas a horizontal position or raising the legs can worsen the casualty's condition. (First-aid rules)

g10-q2.text: At a traffic crash, which of the following injured persons should receive assistance first?
options: A man with a fractured arm.
g10-q2.explanation: During a car accident, priority aid is given to an unconscious casualty in an immediately life-threatening condition, as it is urgent to check their breathing and clear the airways. Fear, scrapes, and an upper-arm fracture do not pose an immediate fatal danger and wait second in line. (First-aid rules)

g10-q3.text: When providing first aid for a nosebleed, you should:
options: Tilt the person’s head forward and pinch the upper part of the nose.
Place a cotton swab in the person’s nose.
Allow the bleeding to continue until it stops on its own.
g10-q3.explanation: In case of a nosebleed, the casualty's head should be tilted slightly forward and the upper soft part of the nose pinched with the fingers. When tilting the head back, blood flows into the throat and can cause choking or vomiting, while inserting a tampon or letting it bleed freely does not stop the bleeding and is dangerous. (First-aid rules)

g10-q4.text: While driving, the driver suddenly begins complaining of severe pressure-like chest pain and difficulty breathing. What should be done?
options: Advise the driver to go to the nearest hospital.
Give the driver a glass of water and two valerian tablets.
Stop the vehicle immediately and activate the hazard warning lights.
Advise the driver to walk a little and breathe fresh air.
g10-q4.explanation: Severe crushing chest pain and difficulty breathing are signs of an acute heart muscle problem, so it is necessary to immediately stop the car and turn on the hazard lights, preventing an accident and additional strain. Driving to the hospital oneself or walking strains the heart, while giving pills or water during first aid is prohibited. (First-aid rules)

g10-q5.text: What assistance should be provided to a person having a seizure?
options: Hold the person and try to restrain the convulsions.
Try to open the mouth, hold the tongue, and place an object between the teeth.
Try to open the airway by tilting the person’s head back.
Do not interfere; allow the seizure to end.
g10-q5.explanation: During a seizure, do not touch the casualty and let the convulsions end (removing only nearby dangerous objects). Forcibly restraining convulsions can cause injuries, while prying open the mouth and inserting an object breaks teeth and blocks the airways. (First-aid rules)

g10-q6.text: What should be done when providing first aid for a burn?
options: Open the fluid-filled blisters and then apply a tight bandage.
Cool the burn with water, then cover it with sterile dressing material or clean cloth.
g10-q6.explanation: In case of a burn, the first step is to cool the damaged surface with cold water, after which it should be covered with a sterile bandage or clean cloth to protect against infection. Popping blisters and applying oil deepen tissue damage and the risk of infection, while leaving it uncovered increases pain and contamination. (First-aid rules)

g10-q7.text: As a result of a crash, a pedestrian has fallen and injured an arm. There is a large wound on the forearm (about 5 cm long) from which dark-colored blood is flowing steadily. What should be done to stop the bleeding?
options: Raise the injured person’s arm and apply a pressure bandage.
Apply an alcoholic iodine solution to the wound.
g10-q7.explanation: Dark blood flowing steadily from a wound is a sign of venous bleeding, which is stopped by raising the casualty's arm and applying a pressure bandage over the wound. Washing the wound with water or applying iodine increases bleeding and damages open tissues. (First-aid rules)

g10-q8.text: When providing first aid during the first hours after a closed soft-tissue injury to a limb, you should:
options: Apply a warm compress to the injury.
Apply a cold compress to the injured area and elevate it.
Apply a cold compress to the injured area and keep it below heart level.
Apply an alcohol compress to the injury.
g10-q8.explanation: For closed soft-tissue injuries of the limbs, during the first hours apply a cold compress and elevate the injured limb to reduce swelling and internal bleeding. Warming or alcohol compresses, or keeping the limb below heart level, dilate blood vessels and increase swelling and pain. (First-aid rules)

g10-q9.text: A driver had been crouching for a long time while changing a vehicle’s wheel. After suddenly standing up, the driver grabs the head, loses consciousness, and falls. What should be done?
options: Pour cold water on the driver’s face.
g10-q9.explanation: Loss of consciousness after standing up abruptly (fainting) is caused by a temporary decrease in blood flow to the brain, so you should lay the casualty down and raise their legs. Sitting them up worsens brain blood supply, while slapping or pouring cold water is useless and can harm the casualty. (First-aid rules)

g10-q10.text: What should be done if the scene cannot be made safe?
options: Provide assistance to everyone, but be careful.
Provide assistance to the injured person who is closest to you.
Do not approach; immediately call for emergency assistance and prevent bystanders from approaching the scene.
Do not approach; ask someone else to provide assistance.
g10-q10.explanation: The main rule of first aid is the rescuer's safety: if scene safety cannot be ensured, do not approach; instead, immediately alert specialists and prevent bystanders from entering the danger zone. Entering the danger zone or sending others in can increase the number of casualties. (First-aid rules)

g10-q11.text: You see a person lying on the ground and notice a bone protruding from the lower leg with bleeding. If the scene is safe, what should be done first?
g10-q11.explanation: Once the scene is already safe, regardless of a visible fracture or blood, first check the casualty's consciousness and breathing. Only after assessing vital functions are calling an ambulance and immobilizing the limb performed. (First-aid rules)

g10-q12.text: When an injured person has an open fracture of a limb, first aid requires you to:
options: Cover the wound with a sterile dressing and immobilize the injured limb.
Stop the bleeding by direct pressure.
Apply cold compresses to the wound.
g10-q12.explanation: In the event of an open fracture, cover the wound with a sterile pad to prevent infection and carefully immobilize the injured limb. Raising the limb or applying direct pressure over the wound can displace bone fragments and damage blood vessels and nerves, while a cold compress does not protect against infection. (First-aid rules)

g10-q13.text: In case of a chest injury, you should:
options: Lay the injured person in a horizontal position.
Seat the injured person, supporting the injured side.
Seat the injured person, supporting the uninjured side.
g10-q13.explanation: In case of a chest injury, the casualty should be seated leaning toward the injured side, which limits movement and pain on the injured side and ensures full breathing of the healthy lung. A horizontal position and leaning on the healthy side make breathing difficult. (First-aid rules)

g10-q14.text: If organs protrude through an open abdominal wound, you should:
options: Wash them and carefully try to place the protruding organs back inside.
Cover the protruding organs with a clean moist cloth and plastic film.
Cut off the protruding organs and bandage the wound.
Do not touch them; transport the injured person to a hospital in that condition.
g10-q14.explanation: If organs protrude from an open abdominal wound, they must not be pushed back inside or cut; instead, cover them with a clean damp cloth and polyethylene film to protect against drying and infection. Leaving them uncovered or attempting to push them back causes severe infection and fatal complications. (First-aid rules)

g10-q15.text: An unconscious injured person who is breathing should be:
options: Have the mouth opened and the tongue pulled out.
Turned onto the side with the head tilted back.
g10-q15.explanation: An unconscious casualty who is breathing must be turned into the stable side (recovery) position with the head tilted slightly back, ensuring airway patency and preventing the tongue from falling back or inhaling vomit. Leaving them on their back or forcibly opening the mouth and pulling the tongue are dangerous and incorrect actions. (First-aid rules)

g10-q16.text: In case of severe bleeding, you should:
options: Only cover the wound with a bandage.
Apply a pressure bandage to the injured area and apply pressure at the arterial pressure point.
g10-q16.explanation: To stop severe bleeding, bandage the injured part with pressure and press the corresponding arterial pressure point. An ordinary loose bandage does not stop blood flow, while pouring ash or other substances causes severe wound infection. (First-aid rules)

g10-q17.text: In case of a motor-vehicle crash, the first action should be to:
options: Place the injured person in a comfortable position.
Assess the scene and ensure safety.
Check the injured person for severe bleeding.
Remove the injured person from the vehicle.
g10-q17.explanation: In a car accident, first inspect the scene and ensure safety (turn on hazard lights, place the warning triangle, assess the risk of fire or secondary run-over). Approaching, moving, or positioning the casualty without checking safety endangers both the rescuer's and the casualty's lives. (First-aid rules)

g10-q18.text: If there is a foreign object in the injured person’s wound, first aid requires you to:
options: Remove the foreign object from the wound.
Allow the injured area to bleed.
Treat the area around the wound with alcohol.
g10-q18.explanation: If there is a foreign object in the wound, when giving aid ensure it remains immobilized (by securing around it with a bandage). Removing a foreign object can cause life-threatening bleeding and further tissue damage, while treating with alcohol or leaving it bleeding is dangerous. (First-aid rules)

g10-q19.text: At rest, an adult’s pulse rate is:
g10-q19.explanation: At rest, the normal pulse of an adult is 60–80 beats per minute. 40–60 beats is a sign of a slow pulse, while 80–100 beats exceeds the average resting norm. (First-aid rules)

g10-q20.text: At rest, an adult’s respiratory rate is:
g10-q20.explanation: At rest, the normal breathing rate of an adult is 12–18 breaths per minute. 20–30 or 40–60 breaths are characteristic of children or of shortness of breath and respiratory disorders. (First-aid rules)

g10-q21.text: After a crash, an injured person should be removed from the vehicle if:
options: The injured person has serious injuries.
The scene is dangerous, for example, there is a risk of explosion.
An electrical wire has fallen onto the vehicle.
g10-q21.explanation: In an accident, a casualty should be moved from a car only if there is an immediate threat to life, such as a risk of explosion or fire. During serious injuries, unnecessary movement can worsen spinal or bone damage, and when a power line has fallen, approaching the car is prohibited until the power is switched off. (First-aid rules)

g10-q22.text: If internal abdominal bleeding is suspected, first aid requires you to:
options: Lay the injured person down and apply a cold compress to the injured area.
Apply a hot-water bottle to the abdomen.
Apply a pressure bandage to the abdomen.
Give the injured person a large amount of fluid.
g10-q22.explanation: If internal abdominal bleeding is suspected, lay the casualty down and place a cold compress on the abdomen to constrict blood vessels and reduce bleeding. A hot-water bottle, pressure bandage, and giving fluids worsen bleeding and internal organ damage. (First-aid rules)

g10-q23.text: You hear a vehicle engine running in your neighbor’s garage. When you open the door, you see your neighbor lying on the floor. What should you do first?
options: Open the doors wide and turn off the engine; if possible, remove the injured person from the scene.
Carefully examine the injured person’s body for injuries.
Turn the injured person onto the side into the recovery position.
Help the injured person into a semi-sitting position.
g10-q23.explanation: A running engine in a closed garage creates a fatal risk of carbon monoxide poisoning, so first open the doors wide, turn off the engine, and if possible carry the casualty out into fresh air. Examining or positioning without ventilating the space endangers the rescuer's life as well. (First-aid rules)

g10-q24.text: After finding an unconscious injured person, the first action should be to:
options: Turn the person onto the side into the recovery position.
Maintain the person’s normal body temperature.
Open the airway and check for breathing.
g10-q24.explanation: After finding an unconscious casualty, first open the airways and check breathing to assess the need for cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Giving water to an unconscious person is prohibited due to the risk of choking, and turning onto the side is allowed only after confirming breathing. (First-aid rules)

g10-q25.text: To check circulation in an injured limb, press and release the nail below the bandage. Circulation in the limb is impaired if:
options: The nail is difficult to blanch when pressed.
The nail is slow to return to a pink color.
g10-q25.explanation: Pressing and releasing a fingernail checks capillary refill: if the nail has difficulty turning pink again, blood circulation in the limb is impaired (for example, from an overly tight bandage). Pain, restlessness, or difficulty turning white when pressed are not the criteria of this check. (First-aid rules)

g10-q26.text: Your friend with diabetes feels unwell and cannot remember when insulin was last taken. What should you do first?
options: Give the person sugar or a sweet drink.
g10-q26.explanation: When a diabetic feels unwell and the time of insulin intake is unknown, first give sugar or a sweet liquid, as a sharp drop in blood sugar (hypoglycemia) quickly threatens life and is safely corrected with sweets. Leaving them alone or injecting insulin can lead to a coma. (First-aid rules)

options: The blood spurts from the wound.
The blood flows steadily from the wound.
g10-q27.explanation: Bleeding is most dangerous when blood spurts in a jet from the wound, which indicates arterial bleeding. Under high pressure, blood flows out very rapidly and causes fatal blood loss in a short time—unlike dark, steadily flowing venous bleeding. (First-aid rules)

g10-q28.text: A vehicle has struck a utility pole, and an electrical wire has fallen onto an unconscious injured person lying beside the vehicle. When providing assistance, the first action should be to:
options: Remove the injured person from the source of electrical current.
Remove the wire from the injured person using an insulating object.
Look for electrical entry and exit points (burns) on the body.
g10-q28.explanation: If an electrical wire has fallen onto a casualty, first move the wire off the casualty using an insulating (dry wooden or plastic) object, de-energizing the danger zone. Touching, pulling, or examining the casualty without removing the wire will electrocute the rescuer as well. (First-aid rules)

g10-q29.text: When providing first aid, to protect yourself from infection, you should:
options: Avoid direct contact with the wound and provide assistance only while wearing sterile gloves.
Do not assist injured persons who are bleeding.
g10-q29.explanation: To protect against infection, avoid touching the wound directly and provide aid only while wearing sterile medical gloves. This protects both the casualty from wound contamination and the rescuer from blood-borne infections, whereas refusing to help a bleeding casualty is unacceptable. (First-aid rules)

g10-q30.text: During an asthma attack, an injured person with bronchial asthma should be:
options: Laid down with the legs elevated.
Laid down with the knees bent.
Laid down with the head elevated.
g10-q30.explanation: During a bronchial asthma attack, help the casualty assume a semi-sitting position with elbows resting on their knees or a convenient support, which eases the work of the respiratory muscles. Lying down or raising the legs increases pressure on the chest and worsens suffocation. (First-aid rules)

g10-q31.text: An injured person with an abdominal injury should be:
options: Laid down with the head elevated.
Laid down with the legs elevated.
Laid down with the knees bent.
g10-q31.explanation: A casualty with an abdominal injury should be laid on their back with knees bent, which relaxes tension in the anterior abdominal wall muscles and eases pain. Keeping the head elevated or lifting the legs up can increase intra-abdominal pressure. (First-aid rules)

g10-q32.text: In the event of fainting, the injured person should be:
options: Laid down with the legs elevated.
Laid down with the knees bent.
Laid down with the head elevated.
g10-q32.explanation: In case of fainting, lay the casualty on their back and raise their legs to ensure rapid blood flow to the brain. Semi-sitting or head-elevated positions worsen the brain's blood deficit, while bending the knees is used mainly for abdominal injuries. (First-aid rules)

g10-q33.text: If a low-front vehicle strikes an adult pedestrian who is 1.55 m or taller, injuries are most likely to occur in the:
g10-q33.explanation: In a collision between a low-bodied car and an adult pedestrian 1 m 55 cm or taller, the front of the car strikes the lower limbs, and the body is thrown onto the hood or windshield, causing a head injury. Therefore, a direct impact to the pelvis and chest is less likely in this case. (First-aid rules)

g10-q34.text: If a low-front vehicle strikes a child 3–5 years old, injuries are most likely to occur in the:
g10-q34.explanation: In a collision between a low-bodied car and a 3–5-year-old child, because the child's height is small, the car's front bumper and hood strike mainly the pelvic and chest regions. The typical mechanism of lower-limb and head injuries is characteristic of taller adults. (First-aid rules)

g10-q35.text: If an electrical wire has fallen onto a vehicle, you should:
options: Help the occupants get out of the vehicle immediately.
Ask the occupants to remain in the vehicle until the electrical current is disconnected.
g10-q35.explanation: If an electrical wire has fallen onto a car, ask those inside the vehicle to remain inside until the power is switched off. The car's interior is protected, whereas when exiting, a person may simultaneously touch the car and the ground and suffer a fatal electric shock. (First-aid rules)

g10-q36.text: When treating minor wounds, you should:
options: Wash the wound with soap and clean water, then bandage it.
Treat the wound with alcohol-containing substances (iodine, vodka, perfume, etc.).
g10-q36.explanation: When treating minor (superficial) wounds, wash them with soap and clean water to remove dirt and bacteria, then cover with a bandage. Alcohol-containing substances (iodine, vodka, cologne) burn and damage open tissues, slowing wound healing. (First-aid rules)

g10-q37.text: When treating serious wounds, you should:
options: Wash the wound with soap and clean water.
Treat the wound with alcohol-containing substances (iodine, vodka, perfume, etc.).
Stop the bleeding and bandage the wound.
g10-q37.explanation: For dangerous (deep, heavily bleeding) wounds, the priority is to stop the bleeding and bandage the wound. Washing such wounds with water or treating them with alcohol washes away formed clots, increases bleeding, and damages tissues. (First-aid rules)

g10-q38.text: In case of a crash, what information should be provided to the emergency dispatcher when requesting an ambulance?
options: State the landmark nearest to the crash location. Report the number of injured persons and indicate their sex and age.
State the street and house number nearest to the crash location. Indicate who was injured in the crash (pedestrian, driver, or passenger) and describe the injuries sustained.

State the crash location (street, house number, and the landmarks nearest to the scene). Report the number of injured persons, their sex, approximate age, state of consciousness, breathing and circulation, and whether there is severe bleeding, fractures, or other injuries. Wait until the dispatcher confirms that the call has been received.
g10-q38.explanation: When calling an ambulance, inform the operator of the exact accident location and landmarks, number of casualties, sex, approximate age, vital condition and injuries, and wait for confirmation that the call has been accepted. Shorter versions do not provide enough information for the proper crew composition and rapid arrival. (First-aid rules)

g10-q39.text: What is the optimal position for a conscious injured person when a spinal injury is suspected?
options: Lay the injured person on their side.
Lay the injured person on their back on a firm, flat surface; do not move them or change their position unless necessary.
Lay the injured person on their back, place a roll made from clothing under the neck, and raise the legs.
g10-q39.explanation: If a spinal injury is suspected, a conscious casualty should be laid on their back on a hard, flat surface and, without extreme necessity, should not be moved or have their position changed. Turning onto the side, placing a roll under the neck, or raising the legs can displace vertebrae and damage the spinal cord, causing paralysis. (First-aid rules)

g10-q40.text: How should first aid be provided in case of frostbite and hypothermia?
options: Rub the affected areas of the body with snow or a woolen cloth, then warm them, give the injured person an alcoholic drink, and move them to a warm place.
Warm and immobilize the affected areas of the body, cover the injured person with warm clothing or a blanket, give a warm drink, and move the person to a warm place.
Apply ointment to the affected areas of the body, apply a warming compress and a heating pad, move the injured person to a warm place, and give a warm drink.
g10-q40.explanation: In case of frostbite and hypothermia, move the casualty to a warm room, cover with warm clothes or a blanket, give a warm drink, gradually warm and immobilize the affected parts. Rubbing with snow or wool damages frozen skin, alcohol deepens heat loss, and ointments or a hot-water bottle damage tissues through sudden heating. (First-aid rules)

g10-q41.text: What first aid should be provided for a head injury with a scalp wound?
options: Stop the bleeding by applying direct pressure to the wound and apply a pressure bandage. If the injured person loses consciousness, place them in the recovery position. If possible, apply a cold compress to the injured area of the head.

Immobilize the cervical spine using an improvised splint (collar). Place a sterile cotton pad over the wound and lay the injured person on their back with the legs raised. If possible, apply a cold compress to the head.
A cervical splint must not be applied. Cover the wound with medical adhesive tape and lay the injured person on their side.
g10-q41.explanation: For a scalp wound and craniocerebral injury, stop the bleeding with direct pressure and a pressure bandage, apply cold, and if unconscious place in the stable side (recovery) position. Raising the legs increases intracranial bleeding, cotton sticks to the wound, and simply sticking an adhesive plaster does not stop bleeding. (First-aid rules)

g10-q42.text: When providing first aid to an unconscious injured person who has circulation and breathing, in what position should the person be placed?
options: On their back, with a roll placed under the head.
On their back, with the legs spread apart.
Place the injured person in the recovery position so that the bent knees touch the ground and the upper hand is positioned under the cheek.
g10-q42.explanation: An unconscious casualty with breathing and circulation should be placed in the stable side (recovery) position with bent knees and the upper hand placed under the cheek. When lying on the back, the tongue may fall back and block the airways, or the casualty may choke on vomit. (First-aid rules)

g10-q43.text: How long may a tourniquet used to stop bleeding remain in place?
options: In warm weather, no more than half an hour; in cold weather, no more than one hour.
In warm weather, no more than one hour; in cold weather, no more than half an hour.
There is no limit on how long the tourniquet may remain in place.
g10-q43.explanation: A hemostatic tourniquet may remain applied for no more than 1 hour in warm weather, and no more than half an hour in cold weather. Keeping it on longer or failing to observe the time limit leads to irreversible tissue necrosis in the limb. (First-aid rules)

g10-q44.text: How should you determine whether an unconscious injured person is breathing?
options: Hold the injured person by the chin, tilt the head back, and observe chest movement for 10 seconds.

Place one hand on the injured person’s forehead and, with two fingers of the other hand, lift the chin and tilt the head back. For 10 seconds, check for breathing by trying to feel exhaled air on your cheek and observing movement of the chest.
Without tilting the injured person’s head, lean toward the person’s face and, for 10 seconds, check for breathing by trying to feel exhaled air on your cheek and observing movement of the chest.
g10-q44.explanation: To check the breathing of an unconscious casualty, place one hand on the forehead, lift the chin with two fingers of the other hand (opening the airways), and for 10 seconds follow the "look, listen, feel" principle for chest movement and exhaled air. Without tilting the head back, the airways may be closed, and merely looking at the chest can give a false result. (First-aid rules)

g10-q45.text: What are the main signs of severe arterial bleeding, and what action should be taken first when providing first aid in such a situation?
options: Dark-colored blood slowly flows from the wound. Apply a pressure bandage to the wound and note on it how long it should remain in place.

Bright red blood spurts forcefully from the wound in an intermittent jet or fountain-like stream. Compress the injured artery with your fingers, then apply a tourniquet above the wound, as close to the wound as possible, and note the time it was applied.
Blood slowly flows from the wound. Apply a tourniquet below the injury and note the time it was applied.
g10-q45.explanation: During major arterial bleeding, bright red blood spurts in an intermittent jet: as a first step, press the artery with your fingers, then above the wound—as close to the wound as possible—apply a tourniquet, noting the time of application. The first option describes venous bleeding, and a tourniquet placed below the wound does not stop arterial flow. (First-aid rules)

g10-q46.text: Is it permitted to give medication to an injured person while providing first aid?
options: Permitted in case of extreme necessity.
g10-q46.explanation: Giving medications to a casualty while administering first aid is prohibited. Without a medical examination, it is impossible to rule out allergic reactions, contraindications, or a misassessment of the condition, which can worsen the casualty's state. (First-aid rules)

g10-q47.text: How should bleeding be stopped in case of injury to veins or small arteries?
options: Apply a pressure bandage directly over the injured area.
Apply a pressure bandage above the wound.
Apply a pressure bandage below the wound.
g10-q47.explanation: In the event of injury to veins and non-major arteries, bleeding is stopped directly at the injury site by applying a pressure bandage over the wound. A bandage placed above or below the wound does not compress the damaged vessel and does not stop the bleeding. (First-aid rules)

g10-q48.text: For injuries sustained in a crash, what are the initial first-aid steps?
options: Rinse the wound with water, remove foreign objects from the wound, place sterile cotton on the wound, and secure it with a bandage.
Put on medical gloves, clean the wound with an alcohol solution of iodine, apply medicated ointment, and cover it with adhesive tape.
Put on medical gloves and, without cleaning the wound, cover it with a sterile gauze pad, securing the edges with adhesive tape or a bandage.
g10-q48.explanation: The initial first-aid steps for accident wounds are: put on medical gloves, cover the wound without cleaning it using a sterile gauze pad, and secure it with adhesive tape or a bandage. Washing with water, removing a foreign body, using iodine or ointment, and placing cotton directly on the wound damage tissues and cause complications. (First-aid rules)

g10-q49.text: How should first aid be provided for limb fractures when no splints or materials for making a splint are available?
options: Secure the upper limb to the torso with the arm extended along the body. Tie the lower limbs together, placing soft material between them.
With the upper limb bent at the elbow and supported in a sling, secure it to the torso. Tie the lower limbs together, placing soft material between them.
With the upper limb bent at the elbow and supported in a sling, secure it to the torso. Tie the lower limbs together.
g10-q49.explanation: When no splints are on hand, bend the upper limb at the elbow joint, support it in a triangular sling and tie it to the torso, and tie the lower limbs to each other with soft cloth placed between them. Tying an extended arm does not provide comfortable immobilization, while not placing soft cloth between the legs causes bone friction and pain. (First-aid rules)

g10-q50.text: In which cases should an injured person be removed from the vehicle?
options: If the vehicle has overturned, caught fire, there is a high risk of explosion, or the injured person has lost consciousness.

If the vehicle has overturned, caught fire, there is a high risk of explosion, or the injured person has hypothermia, has lost consciousness or breathing, or it is impossible to provide first aid directly inside the vehicle.
If the vehicle has overturned, caught fire, there is a high risk of explosion, or the injured person has severe bleeding or a head injury.
g10-q50.explanation: A casualty should be removed from the car cabin only when there is a high probability of the vehicle overturning, catching fire, or exploding, casualty hypothermia, loss of consciousness and breathing, or impossibility of providing first aid inside the cabin. In the case of bleeding or a craniocerebral injury alone without the listed dangers, moving may cause further harm to the casualty. (First-aid rules)

g10-q51.text: When providing first aid for a superficial thermal burn (skin redness, swelling, blisters filled with clear fluid at the burn site, and severe pain), what should be done?
options: Pour cold water over the burned area, cover it with a sterile pad, and bandage it tightly.
Open the blisters, remove clothing remnants from the burned area, cover it with a sterile pad without bandaging it, apply a cold compress if possible, and give the injured person water to drink.

Cool the burned area with water for 20 minutes. Without opening the blisters or removing clothing remnants, cover the burned area with a sterile pad without bandaging it, apply a cold compress if possible, and give the injured person water to drink.
g10-q51.explanation: For a superficial thermal burn, cool the surface with water for 20 minutes, without popping blisters or tearing off clothing cover it with a sterile pad (do not bandage), apply cold if possible, and give water to drink. Tightly bandaging, popping blisters, or removing stuck clothing deepens the injury and introduces infection. (First-aid rules)
